\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic denominator-layer theorem]
\label{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
For a finite word \(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\) of positive integers, let
\(\mathcal K(\mathbf a)\) be its regular continuant, with
\[
 \begin{gathered}
  \mathcal K(\varnothing)=1,\qquad \mathcal K(a_1)=a_1,\\
  \mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)
  =a_r\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1})
   +\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-2}).
 \end{gathered}
\]
Put
\[
 \begin{aligned}
  \mathcal C_{\rm L}&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
   \bigcup_{r\ge1}\mathbb N^r,\\
  \mathcal C_{\rm R}&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
   \{(a_1,\ldots,a_r):r\ge1,\ a_i\ge1,\ a_r\ge2\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Then, for every fixed \(s>2\),
\begin{equation}
 b_{2d+1}(s)\sim b(s)d^{-s}\qquad(d\to\infty),
 \label{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}
\end{equation}
where the constant is the absolutely convergent one-large-partial-quotient
context sum
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 b(s)
 &: =\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
       \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}
       \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\\
 &=2\left(\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}\right)^2>0.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}
\end{equation}
In particular, this identifies the polynomial scale of every fixed
low-temperature denominator layer; no tail hypothesis is used in
\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write \(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\), with
\(|\varnothing|_1=0\).  The canonical regular continued fraction of a reduced
\(p/q\in(0,1)\) is
\[
 \frac pq=[0;a_1,\ldots,a_r],
 \qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_r\ge2,
\]
and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\).  The conversion formula
used in the proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} gives
\[
 d(p/q)=|\mathbf a|_1-1.
\]
Consequently, on putting \(n=d+1\), the left side of
\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer} is
\begin{equation}
 A_n(s):=
 \sum_{\substack{\mathbf a\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\|\mathbf a|_1=n}}
 \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-s}.
 \label{eq:regular-continuant-layer}
\end{equation}

We first evaluate the context mass.  Canonical words in
\(\mathcal C_{\rm R}\) with
denominator \(q\) parameterize the \(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in
\((0,1)\).  Hence, for \(s>2\),
\begin{equation}
 R_s:=\sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}\mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s}
 =1+\sum_{q\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(q)}{q^s}
 =\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}<\infty.
 \label{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}
\end{equation}
Every nonempty positive word either ends in a digit at least two or has the
form \((a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)\).  The usual terminal move
\[
 (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)
 \longleftrightarrow
 (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1}+1)
\]
preserves the continuant.  It pairs the two regular expansions of every
nonempty canonical word; it also pairs \((1)\) with \(\varnothing\).  Therefore
\begin{equation}
 L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}\mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
 =2R_s.
 \label{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}
\end{equation}
This proves the absolute convergence and the evaluation in
\eqref{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}.

It remains to prove that this context sum is the whole local main term.  We
give the cutoff argument, including the multiple-large-digit and moderate
parts.  The continuant concatenation formula implies, for finite positive
words \(\mathbf u,\mathbf v\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal K(\mathbf u\mathbf v)
 \ge \mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v).
 \label{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound}
\end{equation}
Moreover, with the two contexts fixed and \(a\to\infty\), multilinearity of
the tridiagonal determinant defining the continuant gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)
 =a\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)+O_{\mathbf u,\mathbf v}(1).
 \label{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine}
\end{equation}

Let \(P_n(s)\) be the part of \eqref{eq:regular-continuant-layer} coming from
words having a digit greater than \(n/2\).  Such a digit is unique.  Cutting
there is a bijection with pairs
\((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\times\mathcal C_{\rm R}\)
satisfying
\(|\mathbf u|_1+|\mathbf v|_1<n/2\), the middle digit being
\(a=n-|\mathbf u|_1-|\mathbf v|_1\).  Equations
\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} and
\eqref{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine} give, respectively,
\[
 n^s\mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)^{-s}
 \le 2^s\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}
\]
and pointwise convergence of the left side to
\(\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\).  Dominated
convergence, using \eqref{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}--
\eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, therefore yields
\begin{equation}
 n^sP_n(s)\longrightarrow L_sR_s=b(s).
 \label{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}
\end{equation}

We now show that the complementary words have total weight \(o(n^{-s})\).
Choose
\begin{equation}
 \frac{s}{2(s-1)}<\delta<1,
 \qquad h=\lfloor n^\delta\rfloor,
 \label{eq:large-digit-cutoff}
\end{equation}
and set
\[
 \eta_s(h):=
 \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
 \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
\]
By \eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).  A word having
at least two digits not smaller than \(h\) can be cut at its first two such
digits.  After dropping the restrictions on the three intervening contexts,
\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} bounds its total weight by
\begin{equation}
 L_s^2R_s
 \left(\sum_{a\ge h}a^{-s}\right)^2
 =O_s(h^{2-2s})=o(n^{-s}),
 \label{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}
\end{equation}
where the last equality is precisely the first inequality in
\eqref{eq:large-digit-cutoff}.

For completeness, consider a word all of whose digits are smaller than
\(h\).  Greedily divide it into consecutive blocks: close a block as soon as
its digit sum reaches \(h\), and leave the last remainder unclosed.  Every
closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum at least
\(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.  The
concatenation bound and the uniqueness of the greedy decomposition show that
the total continuant weight of all such words is at most
\begin{equation}
 \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
 \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1}
 \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large \(h\).  When \(N\ge n/4\), this is
\(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A>0\), because \(n/h\to\infty\) and
\(\eta_s(h)\to0\).

The words not counted by \(P_n(s)\) and not covered by
\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible} have at most one digit at least \(h\).
If there is none, apply \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} with \(N=n\).  If
there is exactly one, its value is at most \(n/2\), so the two surrounding
moderate contexts have combined digit sum at least \(n/2\); one has digit sum
at least \(n/4\).  Cutting at the exceptional digit, summing its weight
\(a^{-s}\), and applying \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} to that long context
again gives \(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A\).  Together with
\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}, this proves
\[
 A_n(s)-P_n(s)=o(n^{-s}).
\]
Combining this with \eqref{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}, and replacing
\(n=d+1\) by \(d\), proves \eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic critical stable renewal]
\label{thm:arithmetic-critical-stable-renewal}
Put \(\alpha:=\sigma_0-1\in(1,2)\), and under the critical letter law put
\[
 \Pr\{(C,H)=(c(p/q),\log q)\}=q^{-\sigma_0}.
\]
Then \(\Pr\{C=2d+1\}=b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)\), and the explicit constants
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 b_C&:=
 \sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
 \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}
 \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-\sigma_0}
 =2\left(\frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}\right)^2=8,\\
 K_C&:=\frac{2^{\sigma_0-1}}{\sigma_0-1}b_C
 =\frac{2^{\sigma_0+2}}{\sigma_0-1}
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:critical-tail-constants}
\end{equation}
are positive.  The double series defining \(b_C\) is absolutely convergent,
and
\begin{align}
 b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)&\sim b_Cd^{-\sigma_0},
 &&d\to\infty,
 \label{eq:critical-letter-local-tail}\\
 \Pr\{C>x\}
 &=\sum_{q\ge2}q^{-\sigma_0}
   \card{\{1\le p<q:(p,q)=1,\ c(p/q)>x\}},\notag\\
 &\sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0},
 &&x\to\infty.
 \label{eq:critical-letter-tail}
\end{align}
If \(u_j=u_j(\sigma_0)\) is the renewal sequence in
\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-coefficients}, then
\begin{equation}
 u_j=\frac1{\mu_C}
 +\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)}j^{2-\sigma_0}
 +o(j^{2-\sigma_0}).
 \label{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{align}
 Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)
 &=\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
 +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
 \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order}\\
 S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
 &=\frac{4m}{\mu_C}
 +\frac{4K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}).
 \label{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}
\end{align}
Finally, \(C\) belongs to the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive
\(\alpha\)-stable law.  More precisely, if \(a_n>0\) is chosen so that
\(n\Pr\{C>a_n\}\to1\), then for independent copies \(C_1,C_2,\ldots\),
\begin{equation}
 \frac{C_1+\cdots+C_n-n\mu_C}{a_n}
 \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\mathcal S_\alpha,
 \label{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal S_\alpha\) is the spectrally positive \(\alpha\)-stable law
whose L\'evy measure has density \(\alpha x^{-\alpha-1}\) on \((0,\infty)\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The critical equation \eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} makes the displayed
letter law a probability measure.  The local estimate
\eqref{eq:critical-letter-local-tail} and the context-sum evaluation in
\eqref{eq:critical-tail-constants} are \Cref{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
at \(s=\sigma_0\).  Direct summation of that local estimate gives
\[
 \Pr\{C>x\}
 =\sum_{d>(x-1)/2}b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)
 \sim\frac{b_C}{\sigma_0-1}
      \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^{1-\sigma_0},
\]
which is \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail} with the stated \(K_C\).  Thus
regular variation is a conclusion of the arithmetic continuant estimate, not
an assumption.

The distribution of \(C\) has span one, finite mean \(\mu_C\), and tail
\(K_Cj^{-\alpha}\), with \(1<\alpha<2\).  The finite-mean case of the
discrete renewal-sequence theorem \cite{OmeyVanGulck2015} applies.  To make
its constant explicit, write \(\overline F(j)=\Pr\{C>j\}\).  The tail-sum
identity and the Abelian theorem for power series give, as \(z\uparrow1\),
\begin{align*}
 1-B_{\sigma_0}(z)
 &=(1-z)\sum_{j\ge0}\overline F(j)z^j,\\
 \sum_{j\ge0}\overline F(j)z^j
 &=\mu_C+K_C\Gamma(1-\alpha)(1-z)^{\alpha-1}
   +o((1-z)^{\alpha-1}).
\end{align*}
Since \(U_{\sigma_0}(z)=\{1-B_{\sigma_0}(z)\}^{-1}\), it follows that
\[
 U_{\sigma_0}(z)
 =\frac1{\mu_C(1-z)}
 -\frac{K_C\Gamma(1-\alpha)}{\mu_C^2}(1-z)^{\alpha-2}
 +o((1-z)^{\alpha-2}).
\]
The cited arithmetic coefficient theorem, using the span-one hypothesis,
transfers this expansion locally.  As
\(\Gamma(2-\alpha)=(1-\alpha)\Gamma(1-\alpha)\), it gives
\[
 u_j-\frac1{\mu_C}
 \sim\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\alpha-1)}j^{1-\alpha};
\]
see also the generating-function remainder argument for the arithmetic
renewal theorem in \cite[Ch.~XI]{Feller1971}.  Substitution of
\(\alpha=\sigma_0-1\) proves
\eqref{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}.  Summing it and using
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^{m-1}j^{2-\sigma_0}
 \sim\frac{m^{3-\sigma_0}}{3-\sigma_0}
\]
in the exact identities \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} and
\eqref{eq:weighted-window-renewal} proves
\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order} and
\eqref{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}; the boundary terms are
\(O(1)=o(m^{3-\sigma_0})\).

Finally, \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail}, finite mean, and the absence of a
negative tail are precisely the one-sided domain-of-attraction conditions for
an \(\alpha\)-stable law with the normalization in
\eqref{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}; see \cite[Ch.~XVII]{Feller1971}.
\end{proof}


 succeeded in 197ms:
\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Let \(F_0=0\), \(F_1=F_2=1\), and
\(F_{j+2}=F_{j+1}+F_j\), and put
\(\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\).  Let \(R(n)\) be the classical Fibonacci
partition function: the number of partitions of \(n\) into distinct
Fibonacci numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Our main
thermodynamic results concern \(R\) on the standard layers
\[
 \mathcal I_m=[F_{m+1}-1,F_{m+2}-1).
\]
The moment pressure for every real tilt and its first-order transition are
already contained, under an affine normalization, in the golden-ratio
Bernoulli-convolution literature \cite{LauNgai1998,FengOlivier2003,Feng2005}.
We make that normalization explicit and use it as the starting point for
finite-window identities, arithmetic critical refinements, and full
large-deviation lower bounds for \(m^{-1}\log R(n)\) under the uniform law on
\(\mathcal I_m\).

A finite-window Zeckendorf fold gives an exact finite model for this standard
object.  A word
\(\omega\in\{0,1\}^m\) determines the raw sum
\[
  N_m(\omega)=\sum_{j=1}^m\omega_jF_{j+1}.
\]
We consider the finite-window fold obtained by reducing this sum modulo
\(F_{m+2}\) and taking the unique legal Zeckendorf word in the visible
window.  If \(d_m(x)\) is the cardinality of the fiber over a legal word
\(x\), the corresponding finite problem is to identify the multiset
\(\{d_m(x):x\in X_m\}\) and its extremal and moment statistics.

The bridge is exact: the complete fiber list is the list of \(R\) on
\(\mathcal I_m\sqcup\mathcal I_{m+1}\).  A second correspondence is an affine
reindexing of a finite subset-sum spectrum.  Both are finite identities and
do not require a normalization transducer.

\subsection{Main results}

Put \(R(n)=0\) for \(n<0\).  Let \(\sigma_0>2\) be the unique solution of
\[
 \frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}=2;
 \qquad \sigma_0=2.4787507857\ldots.
\]
For \(t>-\sigma_0\), let \(P(t)>0\) be the unique solution of
\[
 \sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
 q^t e^{-P(t)c(p/q)}=1,
\]
where \(c(p/q)\) is the odd continued-fraction cost defined before
\Cref{prop:weighted-generator-renewal}, and put \(P(t)=0\) for
\(t\le-\sigma_0\).  Set
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \mu_C:=\sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
 c(p/q)q^{-\sigma_0},\\
 v_c:=\frac{\displaystyle
 \sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
 q^{-\sigma_0}\log q}{\mu_C},
 \qquad
 t_c:=-\sigma_0,\qquad
 \alpha_+:=\frac12\log\varphi.
 \end{gathered}
\]
Define
\[
 Z_m^R(t):=\sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^t.
\]

The arithmetic input at the critical point is a local theorem, rather than a
tail assumption.  For every fixed \(s>2\),
\begin{equation}
 b_{2d+1}(s)
 \sim2\left(\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}\right)^2d^{-s}.
 \label{eq:introduction-low-temperature-layer}
\end{equation}
Its proof cuts a canonical regular continued fraction at its unique large
partial quotient and gives the constant as an absolutely convergent left--right
continuant context sum.  At \(s=\sigma_0\), this constant is \(b_C=8\), and
\begin{equation}
 \Pr\{C>x\}\sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0},
 \qquad K_C=\frac{2^{\sigma_0-1}}{\sigma_0-1}b_C.
 \label{eq:introduction-critical-cost-tail}
\end{equation}
Consequently, \Cref{thm:arithmetic-critical-stable-renewal} proves
\begin{equation}
 Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)
 =\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
 +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}m^{3-\sigma_0}
 +o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
 \label{eq:introduction-standard-critical-second-order}
\end{equation}
with the corresponding coefficient doubled for \(S_{-\sigma_0}(m)\).  The
critical cost also lies in the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive
\((\sigma_0-1)\)-stable law.  Regular variation in these statements is derived
from \eqref{eq:introduction-low-temperature-layer}; it is not assumed.

\begin{theoremA}[One-layer Fibonacci partition thermodynamics]
For every \(t\in\RR\),
\[
 \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log Z_m^R(t)=P(t).
\]
For \(s>\sigma_0\),
\[
 Z_m^R(-s)\longrightarrow
 \frac2{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-1,
\]
whereas \(Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)\sim2m/\mu_C\).  Under the critical Gibbs law
proportional to \(R(n)^{-\sigma_0}\), the normalized log multiplicity and
generating-layer cost converge jointly to \((v_cU,U)\), with \(U\) uniform on
\([0,1]\).

If \(\mathbf N_m\) is uniform on \(\mathcal I_m\), then
\(m^{-1}\log R(\mathbf N_m)\) satisfies a full large deviation principle
with good rate function
\[
 I(\alpha)=\sup_{t\in\RR}\{t\alpha-P(t)+\log\varphi\}.
\]
Its effective domain is \([0,\alpha_+]\), and
\(I(\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha\) on \([0,v_c]\).
\end{theoremA}

This is \Cref{thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics}.  Its pressure assertion
is the Lau--Ngai/Feng spectrum under
\eqref{eq:erdos-pressure-dictionary}; it is included to normalize the critical
finite-size law and the uniform-layer LDP.  The latter statements use the
one-layer orbit weights \(2,1\), rather than a deduction from the two-layer
fiber mixture.

The same renewal representation retains the normalized generating cost
\(B_m^R=m^{-1}\ell_m^R(\mathbf N_m)\).
\Cref{thm:joint-cost-reward-ldp} proves a full LDP for
\((B_m^R,Y_m^R)\).  Its rate is
\[
 J(\beta,\alpha)=
 (1-\beta)\log\varphi+\beta I(\alpha/\beta)
 \quad(0<\beta\le1,\ 0\le\alpha\le\beta\alpha_+),
\]
with \(J(0,0)=\log\varphi\) and \(J=+\infty\) elsewhere.  In particular,
\[
 J(\beta,\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
 \qquad(0\le\alpha\le\beta v_c),
\]
so coexistence is an affine face of the joint rate surface rather than an
artifact of one-dimensional projection.  Fixed-cost exponential tilting
supplies the strictly convex part; an exact one- or two-letter low-reward
suffix fills every sufficiently large remaining cost on the affine face.

For the exact finite-window model, put
\(R^\dagger(n)=R(n)+R(n-1)\).  Let
\[
  \widetilde d_m(n)=[z^n]\prod_{j=1}^m(1+z^{F_j}),
  \qquad 0\le n<F_{m+2}.
\]
For residues modulo \(F_{m+2}\), define
\[
  \pi_m(n)\equiv F_{m+1}n+F_{m+1}-1\pmod{F_{m+2}}.
\]

\begin{theoremB}[Affine fiber--partition correspondence]
For every \(m\ge1\), the map \(\pi_m\) is a permutation and
\[
  d_m^\#(\pi_m(n))
  =\widetilde d_m(n)
  =R^\dagger(n)-R^\dagger(n-F_{m+1})
  \qquad(0\le n<F_{m+2}).
\]
\end{theoremB}

This combines \Cref{thm:affine-transfer,thm:partition-difference}.  It gives a
pointwise correspondence, not only an equality of aggregate moments.

There is also a direct interval description:
\[
 d_m^\#(r)=
 \begin{cases}
 R(F_{m+2}+r),&0\le r\le F_{m+1}-2,\\
 R(r),&F_{m+1}-1\le r<F_{m+2}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The known extremal classification of Koc\'abov\'a, Mas\'akov\'a, and
Pelantov\'a can therefore be transferred exactly after an explicit change of
Fibonacci convention.

\begin{theoremC}[Interval identity and largest fibers]
Let \(D_m=\max_{x\in X_m}d_m(x)\).  Then
\[
 D_0=D_1=1,\qquad D_{2k}=F_{k+2}\ (k\ge0),\qquad
 D_{2k+1}=2F_{k+1}\ (k\ge1),
\]
and \(D_m=D_{m-2}+D_{m-4}\) for every \(m\ge6\).  The maximizing residues,
including the exceptional initial cases, are given in
\Cref{thm:unconditional-extremal-fibers}.
\end{theoremC}

For a real tilt \(t\), put
\[
  S_t(m)=\sum_{x\in X_m}d_m(x)^t.
\]
The identity
\[
  \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log S_t(m)=0
  \qquad(t\le-\sigma_0)
\]
is recorded in \Cref{prop:negative-temperature-freezing} as a finite-layer
recovery of the frozen branch proved by Feng--Olivier and Feng
\cite{FengOlivier2003,Feng2005}.  The renewal coordinates evaluate the
boundary arithmetically and supply the finite-size consequences below.

The fixed-level information is sharper than the exponential pressure.  Put
\(C_m(k)=\card{\{x\in X_m:d_m(x)=k\}}\), and let \(\Psi(k)\) be Weinstein's
number of generating orbits at level \(k\).

\begin{theoremE}[Local spectrum and critical Gibbs law]
For \(m\ge1\), \(C_m(1)=2\), while for \(k\ge2\),
\[
 C_m(k)\le4\Psi(k),
 \qquad C_m(k)=4\Psi(k)\quad(m\ge2k).
\]
For every \(s>\sigma_0\),
\[
 S_{-s}(m)\longrightarrow
 \mathcal Z(s):=\frac4{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-2.
\]
This is the exact convergence range for the unnormalized sums.  The function
\(\mathcal Z\) has a simple pole at \(\sigma_0\), and the corresponding
fiber-level Gibbs measures converge in total variation with explicit
critical logarithmic moments.
At the endpoint itself,
\[
 S_{-\sigma_0}(m)\sim\frac{4m}{\mu_C}.
\]
Under the finite-window Gibbs law proportional to
\(d_m(x)^{-\sigma_0}\), the normalized pair consisting of log multiplicity
and generating-layer cost converges in distribution to
\((v_cU,U)\), where \(U\) is uniform on \([0,1]\).
\end{theoremE}

The complete statements are
\Cref{thm:local-fiber-spectrum,thm:spectral-partition-function,thm:critical-gibbs-spectrum,thm:critical-finite-window-gibbs}.
They separate an unnormalized critical phenomenon inside the region where
the exponential pressure vanishes.

\begin{theoremF}[Orbit growth and arithmetic critical refinements]
With
\[
 \kappa=-\left.\frac{d}{ds}\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}
 \right|_{s=\sigma_0},
\]
one has
\[
 \sum_{k\le x}\Psi(k)\sim
 \frac{x^{\sigma_0}}{\sigma_0\kappa}.
\]
Moreover, if
\(\beta_*=\log\varphi/\log(2/\varphi)=2.2705594539\ldots\), then
\[
 \liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log S_t(m)>0
 \qquad(t>-\beta_*).
\]
At the known critical point \(t_c=-\sigma_0\), the renewal equation becomes
\[
 \sum_{q\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(q)}{q^{\sigma_0}}=1,
 \qquad
 \frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}=2,
\]
and the positive-phase one-sided derivative is the explicitly convergent
ratio
\[
 P'_+(t_c)=
 \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{q\ge2}\phi_{\rm E}(q)q^{-\sigma_0}\log q}
      {\displaystyle\sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
       c(p/q)q^{-\sigma_0}}.
\]
\end{theoremF}

The all-real existence, implicit branch, frozen phase, and derivative corner
come from Feng's spectrum theorem \cite[Thm.~1.3]{Feng2005} and the
Erd\H{o}s-measure phase transition of Feng--Olivier
\cite[Thms.~2.9--2.10 and App.~A]{FengOlivier2003}.  The theorem above retains
only the Tauberian orbit law, the totient evaluation of the critical equation,
and the one-sided critical moment in the present renewal coordinates.

Let \(\mathbf X_m\) be uniformly distributed on \(X_m\), and put
\[
 Y_m=m^{-1}\log d_m(\mathbf X_m).
\]

\begin{theoremG}[Full large deviations across the freezing corner]
The sequence \((Y_m)\) satisfies a large deviation principle with speed
\(m\) and good rate function
\[
 I(\alpha)=\sup_{t\in\RR}\{t\alpha-P(t)+\log\varphi\}.
\]
Its effective domain is \([0,\alpha_+]\), and
\[
 I(\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
 \qquad(0\le\alpha\le v_c).
\]
For every \(0<\alpha<v_c\), the probabilities of shrinking neighborhoods
have the exact exponential rate \(-I(\alpha)\).
\end{theoremG}

The complete statement and proof are given in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp}.
The new orbit-filling step fills both parities of every sufficiently large
target layer while preserving the source multiplicity.

For a fixed finite set of primes, \Cref{prop:prime-support-interface} gives
the exact joint generating function for multiplier exponents and generator
cost and transfers it to \(C_m(k)\) with the active boundary weights
\(4,3,1\).  We do not assert a directional coefficient or quenched-velocity
asymptotic: the needed parameter-uniform smooth-point estimate and uniform
integrability for the unbounded cost are not supplied by the cited ACSV
results.  \Cref{rem:prime-support-local-open-interface} records the exact
remaining analytic input.

The proof of \Cref{prop:negative-temperature-freezing} includes a separate
layer-count lemma transferring Weinstein's convention \(f_j=F_{j+1}\).  It
distinguishes the levels \(k=1,2\), endpoints, early layers, and the eventual
equality asserted in Weinstein's theorem.

The pressure corner prevents a direct full application of the
G\"artner--Ellis theorem: its lower-bound conclusion does not cover slopes
strictly between the one-sided derivatives at \(-\sigma_0\).  The
orbit-filling argument in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp} supplies those missing
local lower bounds and proves the full large deviation principle, with an
affine rate on the coexistence interval.

\subsection{Contribution boundary}

For auditability, the dependency boundary is summarized before the detailed
discussion.
\noindent\textbf{Koc\'abov\'a--Mas\'akov\'a--Pelantov\'a.}
Imported: extremal values and maximizing integers for the ordinary Fibonacci
partition function.  Proved here from that input: exact convention and
interval transfer to all maximizing finite-window residues.

\noindent\textbf{Weinstein.}
Imported: the free generator monoid, multiplier product, orbit decomposition,
and eventual layer stabilization.  Proved here from that input: the uniform
early-layer bound, weighted cost renewal, exact finite-window transfer, and
the prime-support coefficient interface.

\noindent\textbf{Erd\H{o}s measure and Bernoulli convolutions.}
Sidorov--Vershik use Fibonacci numbers
\(F^{\rm SV}_1=1,F^{\rm SV}_2=2\), hence
\(F^{\rm SV}_j=F_{j+1}\) in our convention.  Their level-\(m\) frequency is
therefore exactly
\begin{align*}
 f_m^{\rm SV}(k)
 &=\#\left\{\boldsymbol\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^m:
   \sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_jF_j^{\rm SV}=k\right\}\\
 &=[z^k]\prod_{j=1}^m(1+z^{F_{j+1}})\\
 &=\#\{\omega\in\{0,1\}^m:N_m(\omega)=k\}.
\end{align*}
Thus the difference is the index shift \(F_j^{\rm SV}=F_{j+1}\), not a
different counting object.  They identify \(2^{-m}f_m^{\rm SV}(k)\) with the
finite masses approximating the Erd\H{o}s measure
\cite[Sec.~3]{SidorovVershik1998}.  Hu studied its golden-ratio local dimensions
\cite{Hu1997}; Lau--Ngai gave the exact \(L^q\)-spectrum for \(q>0\)
\cite{LauNgai1998}; Feng--Olivier and Feng gave the complete real spectrum and
the negative first-order transition \cite{FengOlivier2003,Feng2005}.  These
are imported results, not merely related background.

If \(\mu\) denotes the golden-ratio Bernoulli convolution and
\(\tau_\mu(t)\) uses the convention
\(\tau_\mu(t)=\lim \log\sum_I\mu(I)^t/\log|I|\), then the level masses are
\(2^{-m}\) times the finite Fibonacci representation counts.  Since the net
scale is \(\varphi^{-m}\), the exact exponential-rate dictionary is
\begin{equation}
 P(t)=t\log2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi.
 \label{eq:erdos-pressure-dictionary}
\end{equation}
Thus the all-real pressure, its positive implicit branch, the negative frozen
branch, the first-order corner, and the generic Legendre multifractal
description are prior results.  The present paper adds the exact
  finite-window/fiber correspondences, evaluates Feng's implicit critical
  condition as \(\zeta(\sigma_0-1)/\zeta(\sigma_0)=2\), proves the local
  low-temperature denominator-layer law with its explicit continuant context
  constant, obtains the stable second-order critical terms and uniform
  coexistence law, and proves the stated finite-layer nonexposed-slope lower
  bounds.

\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.13\textwidth}p{0.28\textwidth}p{0.22\textwidth}p{0.30\textwidth}@{}}

maximizing residue and finite-window recurrence\\
Pressure recovery & Lau--Ngai, Feng--Olivier, and Feng &
\eqref{eq:erdos-pressure-dictionary} & zeta critical equation and one-sided
critical moment\\
Local layer & Canonical continued-fraction dictionary & regular
continuant contexts & local \(d^{-s}\) law, critical stable tail, and
\(m^{3-\sigma_0}\) correction\\
Theorem E & Weak-Gibbs phase-transition theory & finite-window layer weights
\(4,3,1\) & \(4/\mu_C\), total-variation limit, and finite-window coexistence\\
Theorem F & Weinstein free monoid and Dirichlet series & continued-fraction
cost and totient sum & Tauberian constant and arithmetic critical evaluation\\
Theorem G & G\"artner--Ellis exposed-slope bounds & uniform finite layers &
parity-complete orbit filling at nonexposed slopes\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{Kesseb\"ohmer--Stratmann; Fiala--Kleban--\"Ozl\"uk.}
Imported: Stern--Brocot/Knauf denominator pressure.  It supplies an alternate
derivation of the already known pressure formula in the renewal coordinates
needed for the finite-size arguments.  The polynomial denominator-layer
asymptotic \eqref{eq:introduction-low-temperature-layer}, including its
explicit context constant and the elimination of multiple-large-digit and
moderate-digit contributions, is proved here and is not a pressure
consequence.

\noindent\textbf{Feller; Wiener--Ikehara; G\"artner--Ellis.}
Imported: classical renewal, Tauberian, and exposed-slope large-deviation
tools.  Proved here from those inputs after the arithmetic tail theorem: the
stable second-order critical finite-size laws, uniform coexistence limit, and
orbit-filling lower bounds at nonexposed slopes.

The residue characterization in \Cref{thm:residue-fibers} is a direct
restatement of the fold definition, and \Cref{thm:fourier-inversion} is the
standard character-orthogonality formula.  The finite-window contributions in
\Cref{sec:residue-affine} are the explicit reversal--complement bijection and
affine residue permutation of \Cref{thm:affine-transfer}, together with the
pointwise fiber formula in \Cref{thm:partition-difference}; the latter follows
by truncating the indexed Fibonacci partition generating function.  The
two-interval fiber identity in \Cref{thm:fiber-partition-interval} is also
specific to the finite-window fold.

The values and maximizing residues in
\Cref{thm:unconditional-extremal-fibers} are not a new extremal classification:
they are the exact convention-and-interval transfer of Theorems~4.7 and~5.3 of
Koc\'abov\'a, Mas\'akov\'a, and Pelantov\'a
\cite{KocabovaMasakovaPelantova2005};
\Cref{cor:extremal-fiber-recurrence} is then an immediate Fibonacci-recurrence
consequence.  The additional ingredient in the negative-tilt argument is the
uniform early-layer estimate proved from Weinstein's orbit formulas.  That
estimate, which strengthens eventual layer stabilization to a bound valid in
every layer, yields \Cref{prop:negative-temperature-freezing}.  The local
microcanonical limit and the exact unnormalized
partition function in \Cref{sec:local-spectrum} combine this finite-window
two-layer identity with Weinstein's published orbit decomposition.  The
Wiener--Ikehara theorem itself is classical \cite{Korevaar2004};
\Cref{thm:psi-tauberian} is its application to the specific orbit Dirichlet
series, and \Cref{thm:pressure-transition-strip} is a separate finite-window
Jensen and maximum-level estimate.  Weinstein's free-monoid bijection,
multiplier multiplicativity, orbit decomposition, and largest-index formula
are published
  \cite[Prop.~3.3 and Thms.~3.8, 5.1, and 10.3]{Weinstein2016}; none of
  these mechanisms is claimed here.  The Stern--Brocot/Knauf denominator
  pressure is likewise published.  The weighted length renewal in
  \Cref{prop:weighted-generator-renewal} and its exact finite-window transfer
  are additional steps here; the resulting pressure is the
  Bernoulli-convolution spectrum under \eqref{eq:erdos-pressure-dictionary},
  not a new pressure theorem.  The local denominator-layer theorem
  \Cref{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer} is a separate arithmetic result; its
  proof does not assume the regular variation later used by the renewal
  transfer.
The one-layer pressure, critical Gibbs law, and LDP in
\Cref{thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics} are consequences for the
standard function \(R\) itself.  Their lower-bound proof uses the one-layer
orbit weights directly and does not infer componentwise behavior from the
two-layer fiber mixture.
The standard large-deviation upper bound and the lower bounds at exposed
slopes are separated in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp} from the new finite-window
orbit-filling argument, which supplies the missing lower bounds at the
nonexposed coexistence slopes.
The marked critical renewal identity is a bivariate restatement of
\Cref{prop:weighted-generator-renewal}, whereas its conditional consequences
are additional finite-window results.  The arithmetic renewal theorem and
Blackwell's renewal theorem are classical inputs and are not reproved; the
stable second-order coefficients and uniform coexistence law are their
finite-window transfers through the exact boundary identities after the
critical cost tail has been proved arithmetically.

The separately compiled supplement keeps the conditional arithmetic and
integer-moment consequences outside the main theorem spine.  It labels the
moment constants as transfers of Sanna's theorem and the governing quadratic
cubic as already present in work of Chow and Jones \cite{ChowJones2024}.

\subsection{Related work}

The uniqueness theorem underlying the legal expansion is due to Zeckendorf
\cite{Zeckendorf1972}; Lekkerkerker's work provides classical background on
the same numeration system \cite{Lekkerkerker1952}.  Berstel developed the
normalization and automata viewpoint for Fibonacci representations
\cite{Berstel2001}.  The representation-counting function itself has been
studied through recurrence formulas, partition identities, extremal bounds,
and automata by Carlitz \cite{Carlitz1968}, Robbins \cite{Robbins1996},
Bicknell-Johnson and Fielder \cite{BicknellJohnsonFielder1999}, Stockmeyer
\cite{Stockmeyer2008}, Chow and Slattery \cite{ChowSlattery2021}, and Shallit
\cite{Shallit2021}.  Weinstein's orbit and level-set analysis
\cite{Weinstein2016} and the exact extremal classification of Koc\'abov\'a,
Mas\'akov\'a, and Pelantov\'a \cite{KocabovaMasakovaPelantova2005} are the
specific inputs to \Cref{sec:extremal-ldp}.  Sanna proved the power-sum
asymptotics used here and the endpoint law
\(\lim_{q\to\infty}\lambda_q^{1/q}=\varphi^{1/2}\)
\cite[Thms.~1.1 and~1.2]{Sanna2025}.  Zhou gives a broader treatment of
representation functions for related numeration systems and, in particular,
resolves the logarithmic-average conjecture of Chow and Slattery
\cite[Cor.~1.5]{Zhou2023}.
Chow and Jones obtained the same cubic that appears in the quadratic
finite-window recurrence in their analysis of the variance of the partition
function \cite{ChowJones2024}.
The probabilistic version of these finite counts is the Erd\H{o}s measure:
Sidorov and Vershik identify its level masses as normalized Fibonacci
representation frequencies \cite{SidorovVershik1998}.  Hu's local-dimension
analysis \cite{Hu1997}, Lau and Ngai's exact positive-\(q\) spectrum
\cite{LauNgai1998}, Feng and Olivier's weak-Gibbs phase-transition theorem
\cite{FengOlivier2003}, and Feng's explicit all-real golden-ratio formula
\cite{Feng2005} are the direct priority line for the pressure in this paper.
The Stern--Brocot pressure and its Knauf-model realization are taken from
Kesseb\"ohmer--Stratmann and Fiala--Kleban--\"Ozl\"uk
\cite{KessebohmerStratmann2007,FialaKlebanOzluk2003}.  The earlier
Stern--Brocot multifractal theorem of Kesseb\"ohmer and Stratmann
\cite{KessebohmerStratmann2004} concerns interval growth rates, rather than
Fibonacci partition multiplicities or the finite-window uniform law.  The
critical continued-fraction moment uses the fixed-denominator mean theorem of Panov and
Liehl, as recorded in the quantitative modern treatment of
Aistleitner--Borda--Hauke
\cite{Panov1982,Liehl1983,AistleitnerBordaHauke2023}.

\subsection{Organization}

\Cref{sec:preliminaries} defines the finite-window fold and fixes notation.
\Cref{sec:residue-affine} proves the residue, affine, and partition-difference
formulas.  \Cref{sec:extremal-ldp} proves the interval identity, transfers the
extremal classification, records the finite-layer recovery of the frozen
branch, and isolates the large-deviation interface at the pressure corner.
\Cref{sec:local-spectrum} proves local spectral stabilization, the exact
unnormalized partition function and Gibbs law, the orbit-count Tauberian
asymptotic, the pressure dictionary and arithmetic critical refinements, and
the full large deviation principle across the pressure corner.
\Cref{sec:standard-thermodynamics} proves the one-layer pressure, critical
law, scalar LDP, and joint generation-cost/multiplicity LDP for the classical
Fibonacci partition function itself.
The separately compiled supplement
contains conditional arithmetic refinements, the dyadic ray, and the integer
moment transfer.

This supplement collects three consequences outside the main article's
finite-window phase-transition spine: conditional microcanonical limits,
the exact dyadic multiplier law and its certified speed separation, and
integer-moment transfers with the direct quadratic recurrence.  It uses the
notation and numbered results of the main article.

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

On the standard Fibonacci layer
\(\mathcal I_m=[F_{m+1}-1,F_{m+2}-1)\), the classical partition function
\(R\) has a pressure \(P\) that is exactly the affine normalization
\(P(t)=t\log2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi\) of the known golden-ratio Bernoulli
convolution spectrum.  The all-real spectrum and its first-order transition
are due to Lau--Ngai, Feng--Olivier, and Feng
\cite{LauNgai1998,FengOlivier2003,Feng2005}.  In the renewal coordinates of
this paper one obtains the exact frozen limit
\[
 \sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^{-s}
 \longrightarrow\frac2{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-1
 \qquad(s>\sigma_0),
\]
 and the critical leading law \(2m/\mu_C\).  The arithmetic denominator-layer
 theorem sharpens this to
 \[
  \sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^{-\sigma_0}
  =\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
  +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}m^{3-\sigma_0}
  +o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
 \]
 where \(b_C=8\) is an explicit absolutely convergent continuant context sum
 and \(K_C=2^{\sigma_0-1}b_C/(\sigma_0-1)\).  Its critical Gibbs measure
has the coexistence limit \((v_cU,U)\), and its uniform logarithmic
multiplicity satisfies the full LDP with the affine rate
\(\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha\) on \([0,v_c]\).  These are one-layer theorems
about the standard partition function, not consequences inferred from a
two-layer mixture.

The finite-window fiber spectrum provides an exact finite model and admits
two descriptions.  The affine
permutation \(\pi_m\) identifies each multiplicity with a coefficient of a
finite Fibonacci subset-sum polynomial and with a Fibonacci-lag difference of
the indexed partition function.  The interval identity identifies the same
fiber list with ordinary partition values on two consecutive Fibonacci
layers.  The latter correspondence transfers the published extremal
classification, after an explicit convention change, and yields
\[
 D_{2k}=F_{k+2},\qquad D_{2k+1}=2F_{k+1},\qquad
 D_m=D_{m-2}+D_{m-4}\quad(m\ge6),
\]
together with the complete maximizing-residue list.

For negative real tilts, Weinstein's orbit counts recover the known frozen
half-line and evaluate its critical point arithmetically:
\[
 P(t)=0\qquad(t\le-\sigma_0),
 \qquad
 \frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}=2.
\]
The uniform layer-count lemma treats the two unit conventions, the levels
\(1\) and \(2\), shared endpoints, and early layers explicitly.
At the unnormalized scale, however, the local spectrum stabilizes exactly and
\[
 S_{-s}(m)\longrightarrow
 \frac4{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-2
 \qquad(s>\sigma_0).
\]
This function has a simple pole at \(\sigma_0\), produces an explicit
total-variation Gibbs limit, and yields the Tauberian law
\(\sum_{k\le x}\Psi(k)\sim
x^{\sigma_0}/(\sigma_0\kappa)\).  A separate Jensen lower bound proves
positive lower exponential growth for \(t>-\beta_*\), where
  \(\beta_*=2.2705594539\ldots\).  The weighted free-generator renewal equation,
together with the published Stern--Brocot denominator pressure, gives an
independent derivation in the present finite-layer coordinates of
\[
 \{t:P(t)>0\}=(-\sigma_0,\infty).
\]
The analyticity, strict convexity, and derivative corner on the positive
phase agree with Feng's all-real spectrum.  The renewal coordinates give the
finite positive continued-fraction formula for the right derivative, while
the frozen branch gives the zero left derivative.
At the critical tilt itself, the arithmetic local law and the exact renewal
identity give
\[
 S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
 =\frac{4m}{\mu_C}
 +\frac{4K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}m^{3-\sigma_0}
 +o(m^{3-\sigma_0}).
\]
The input is the proved estimate
\(b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)\sim8d^{-\sigma_0}\), not an assumed regular-variation
hypothesis.  Its one-large-partial-quotient proof controls two large digits
and the all-moderate regime separately, so the local mass has no residual
lattice or semistable oscillation.
The associated finite-window Gibbs measure has a nondegenerate coexistence
limit: the generating-layer fraction is uniform on \([0,1]\), and the
normalized log multiplicity is its product with \(v_c\).

The derivative jump prevents the G\"artner--Ellis theorem alone from treating
the intervening slopes.  A finite-window orbit-filling construction supplies
their matching local lower bounds and proves a full large deviation principle;
its good rate function is affine on the coexistence interval.

On a standard Fibonacci layer, retaining normalized generator cost together
with normalized log multiplicity yields a full two-dimensional large
deviation principle.  Its rate is the perspective of the scalar rate, and its
coexistence region is the affine face
\(J(\beta,\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha\) for
\(0\le\alpha\le\beta v_c\).  The lower bound combines fixed-cost exponential
tilting with an exact low-reward cost filler.

The exact finite-prime-support generating function isolates a remaining
arithmetic boundary.  Its cost-summed coefficients are rational, but the
marked cost has infinite second moment already on the dyadic ray and has no
positive exponential moment.  A directional coefficient law would require
both a parameter-uniform multivariate smooth-point theorem and uniform tail
control for that unbounded cost.  Neither is proved here, so no directional
quenched velocity or active-cutoff asymptotic for \(C_m(k)\) is claimed.

Conditional arithmetic and integer-moment consequences are collected in the
separately compiled supplement.  No transducer-based collision kernel,
algebraicity statement for \(\lambda_q\), arithmetic-window recurrence
polynomial, exact-kernel certificate, Galois group, or Chebotarev density is
claimed in the main article or supplement.

\section{Visible entropy rates and canonical bands}\label{sec:ledger}

Since \(p_m(x)=d_m(x)/2^m\), the visible law under uniform input is the
\(q=1\) canonical ensemble.  With the all-\(q\) asymptotics of \(S_q(m)\) in
hand, we obtain its integer-order R\'enyi entropy rates
\cite{CoverThomas2006} and sharp exponential tail estimates.

\begin{definition}[Visible law under uniform input]
\label{def:visible-law}
For \(m\ge0\), the visible law is the probability measure on \(X_m\) obtained
by pushing the uniform law on \(\Omega_m\) forward by \(\Fold_m\):
\[
  p_m(x):=2^{-m}\card{\{\omega\in\Omega_m:\Fold_m(\omega)=x\}}
  =
  \frac{d_m(x)}{2^m}
  \qquad (x\in X_m).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Typical visible thickness band]
\label{cor:visible-band}
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), let
\[
  B_m(\varepsilon):=
  \left\{
    x\in X_m:
    \Delta_1-\varepsilon\le \frac1m\log d_m(x)
    \le \Delta_2+\varepsilon
  \right\}.
\]
Then
\[
  p_m(B_m(\varepsilon))
  \ge 1-\exp\!\bigl(-(\varepsilon+o(1))m\bigr).
\]
Here \(\Delta_1=\log2-\log\varphi\), because
\(S_1(m)=2^m\) and \(S_0(m)=F_{m+2}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:visible-law},
\[
  p_m(x)=\frac{d_m(x)}{S_1(m)}=\mu_{m,1}(x).
\]
Apply \Cref{thm:gibbs-selection} with \(q=1\).  The two exceptional tails
outside the displayed band each have mass at most
\(\exp(-(\varepsilon+o(1))m)\), and the sum of two such errors is still
\(\exp(-(\varepsilon+o(1))m)\), giving the displayed lower bound for the
band mass.  Finally,
\[
  \Delta_1=P_1-P_0=\log2-\log\varphi,
\]
using \(P_1=\log\lambda_1=\log2\) from \(S_1(m)=2^m\) and
\(P_0=\log\varphi\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Integer-order R\'enyi entropy rates]
\label{thm:renyi-entropy-rate}
\leanverified{paper_projection_renyi_entropy_rate}
For every integer \(q\ge2\), let
\[
  H_q(p_m):=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\sum_{x\in X_m}p_m(x)^q
\]
be the R\'enyi entropy of order \(q\).  Then the entropy rate
\[
  h_q:=\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1mH_q(p_m)
\]
exists and is
\[
  h_q=\frac{q\log2-P_q}{q-1}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
  \lim_{q\to\infty}h_q=\log2-\frac12\log\varphi .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:visible-law},
\[
  \sum_{x\in X_m}p_m(x)^q
  =
  2^{-mq}\sum_{x\in X_m}d_m(x)^q
  =
  2^{-mq}S_q(m).
\]
Therefore
\[
  H_q(p_m)
  =
  \frac{1}{1-q}\bigl(\log S_q(m)-mq\log2\bigr)
  =
  \frac{mq\log2-\log S_q(m)}{q-1}.
\]
For fixed \(q\ge2\), \Cref{thm:all-q-transfer} gives
\[
  \frac1m\log S_q(m)\to P_q,
\]
so the displayed rate follows.  Finally,
\[
  h_q
  =
  \frac{q}{q-1}\log2-\frac{q}{q-1}\cdot\frac{P_q}{q}.
\]
By \Cref{cor:renyi-endpoint}, \(P_q/q=\log(\lambda_q^{1/q})\to
\frac12\log\varphi\), and hence \(h_q\to
\log2-\frac12\log\varphi\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Visible-tail envelope for thick fibers]
\label{cor:visible-thick-tail}
\leanverified{paper_projection_visible_thick_tail}
For \(\alpha\ge0\), set
\[
  E_m(\alpha):=
  \left\{x\in X_m:\frac1m\log d_m(x)\ge\alpha\right\}.
\]
Then, for every integer \(q\ge1\),
\[
  \limsup_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log p_m(E_m(\alpha))
  \le
  P_q-\log2-(q-1)\alpha .
\]
Consequently,
\[
  \limsup_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log p_m(E_m(\alpha))
  \le
  \inf_{q\ge1}\bigl(P_q-\log2-(q-1)\alpha\bigr).
\]
If \(\alpha>\frac12\log\varphi\), then \(p_m(E_m(\alpha))=0\) for all
sufficiently large \(m\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
On \(E_m(\alpha)\), the inequality \(d_m(x)\ge e^{\alpha m}\) gives
\[
  d_m(x)\le e^{-(q-1)\alpha m}d_m(x)^q
  \qquad(q\ge1).
\]
Thus
\[
  p_m(E_m(\alpha))
  =
  2^{-m}\sum_{x\in E_m(\alpha)}d_m(x)
  \le
  2^{-m}e^{-(q-1)\alpha m}S_q(m).
\]
Taking logarithms, dividing by \(m\), and applying
\Cref{thm:all-q-transfer} gives the first bound.  Taking the infimum over
\(q\ge1\) gives the second.  The final assertion follows from
\Cref{thm:max-fiber}: if \(\alpha>\frac12\log\varphi\), then eventually
\(D_m<e^{\alpha m}\), so \(E_m(\alpha)=\varnothing\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Collision entropy rate]
\label{thm:collision-entropy-rate}
\leanverified{paper_projection_collision_entropy_rate}
The collision entropy
\[
  H_2(p_m):=-\log\sum_{x\in X_m}p_m(x)^2
\]
satisfies
\[
  \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1mH_2(p_m)=2\log2-P_2.
\]
Equivalently, \(H_2(p_m)=h_2m+o(m)\) with
\[
  h_2=2\log2-\log\lambda_2.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
This is \Cref{thm:renyi-entropy-rate} with \(q=2\).  Explicitly,
\[
  \sum_{x\in X_m}p_m(x)^2=2^{-2m}S_2(m),
\]
so
\[
  H_2(p_m)=2m\log2-\log S_2(m).
\]
Since \(m^{-1}\log S_2(m)\to P_2=\log\lambda_2\), the asserted rate follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[R\'enyi-2 asymptotics]
\label{cor:renyi2}
Let \(p(\lambda)=\lambda^3-2\lambda^2-2\lambda+2\), and let
\(\lambda_-\in(-2,-1)\), \(\lambda_+\in(0,1)\), and \(\rho\in(2,3)\) be its
three real roots.  With the constants
\[
  T_2(m)=c_\rho\rho^m+c_-\lambda_-^m+c_+\lambda_+^m
\]
from \Cref{thm:q2-alternating-second-order}, one has
\[
  \sum_{x\in X_m}p_m(x)^2
  =
  4^{-m}\bigl(c_\rho\rho^m+c_-\lambda_-^m+c_+\lambda_+^m\bigr),
\]
where \(c_\rho>0\) and \(c_-\ne0\).  In particular,
\[
  \begin{aligned}
  H_2(p_m)
  &=
  m(2\log2-\log\rho)-\log c_\rho\\
  &\quad{}
  -\log\!\left(
    1+\frac{c_-}{c_\rho}\left(\frac{\lambda_-}{\rho}\right)^m
      +\frac{c_+}{c_\rho}\left(\frac{\lambda_+}{\rho}\right)^m
  \right),
  \end{aligned}
\]
and the leading rate is \(2\log2-\log\rho=2\log2-P_2\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:T2}, \(T_2(m)=S_2(m)\).  The exact expansion of \(T_2(m)\) is
\Cref{thm:q2-alternating-second-order}; substituting it into
\[
  \sum_{x\in X_m}p_m(x)^2=4^{-m}S_2(m)
\]
gives the first display.  Since \(\rho\) is the unique dominant root and
\(c_\rho>0\), factor \(c_\rho\rho^m\) out of \(S_2(m)\) and take minus the
logarithm.  This gives the displayed formula for \(H_2(p_m)\).
\Cref{rem:chow-jones} identifies the dominant root \(\rho\) with
\(\lambda_2\), so \(\log\rho=P_2\).
\end{proof}

\ifdefined\supplementonly
\begin{theorem}[Strict dyadic--critical speed separation]
\label{thm:strict-speed-separation}
The dyadic velocity in \Cref{thm:dyadic-exact-multiplier} and the critical
velocity in \Cref{main-thm:full-fiber-ldp} satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
  5.185556312796440793\le\gamma_2
  \le5.235362589164389880,\\
  v_2\ge0.132397168057576261,
 \end{gathered}
 \label{eq:dyadic-speed-certificate}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 v_c\le0.131225207544812100.
 \label{eq:critical-speed-certificate}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 v_2-v_c\ge0.001171960512764161>0.
 \label{eq:strict-speed-separation}
\end{equation}

In particular, fix \(0<\alpha<v_c\), put
\(r_m=\lfloor\alpha m/\log2\rfloor\), and condition uniformly on the exact
level \(d_m=2^{r_m}\).  This level is nonempty for all sufficiently large
\(m\), and
\begin{equation}
 \frac{L(g_m)}m\xrightarrow[m\to\infty]{\Pr}
 \frac{\alpha}{v_2}\ne\frac{\alpha}{v_c}.
 \label{eq:dyadic-uniform-speed-counterexample}
\end{equation}
Thus the critical conditional speed does not extend uniformly from bands to
all realizable exact multiplier sequences.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a reduced fraction \(p/q\in(0,1)\), let \(S(p/q)\) denote the sum of the
partial quotients in its canonical regular continued fraction, so that
\(c(p/q)=2S(p/q)-1\).  Set
\[
 \begin{gathered}
  T(q):=\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}S(p/q),
  \qquad
  \mathcal C(q):=2T(q)-\phi_{\rm E}(q),\\
  A(q):=\sum_{n=1}^{q-1}\tau(n)\tau(q-n).
 \end{gathered}
\]
We first establish an explicit bound for \(\mathcal C(q)\).  Each of the
\(S(p/q)-1\) strict ancestor intervals of \(p/q\) in the Stern--Brocot tree
has ordered adjacent endpoints, say \(a/b<c/d\), and there are unique
positive integers \(u,v\) such that
\[
 \frac pq=\frac{ua+vc}{ub+vd}.
\]
Ordered coprime denominators \(b,d\) determine their Farey adjacent interval
uniquely.  Hence the map from a fraction together with one of its strict
ancestors to \((b,u,d,v)\) is injective, and
\begin{equation}
 T(q)-\phi_{\rm E}(q)\le A(q).
 \label{eq:ancestor-divisor-injection}
\end{equation}
Indeed, the quadruples on the right are counted by factoring
\(n=bu\) and \(q-n=dv\).

Use
\(\tau(n)\le2\sum_{e\mid n,\,e\le\sqrt n}1\), and let
\[
 N_q(e,f):=\card{\{1\le n<q:e\mid n,\ f\mid q-n\}}.
\]
If \(N_q(e,f)>0\), then \((e,f)\mid q\), and the Chinese remainder theorem
gives
\[
 N_q(e,f)\le\frac{q(e,f)}{ef}+1.
\]
Writing \(e=gh\), \(f=gk\), dropping the coprimality of \(h,k\), and using
the harmonic-sum bound gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{e,f\le\sqrt q\\(e,f)\mid q}}
 \frac{(e,f)}{ef}
 \le\sum_{g\mid q}\frac1g
       \left(1+\frac12\log q\right)^2.
\]
For \(q=2^a\), the divisor sum is less than \(2\).  Since there are at most
\(q\) pairs \((e,f)\), it follows that
\[
 A(2^a)\le8\,2^a\left(1+\frac a2\log2\right)^2+4\,2^a.
\]
Combining this with \eqref{eq:ancestor-divisor-injection} and
\(\phi_{\rm E}(2^a)=2^{a-1}\) yields the all-range estimate
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal C(2^a)
 \le2^a\left\{\frac{17}{2}
       +16\left(1+\frac a2\log2\right)^2\right\}
 \qquad(a\ge1).
 \label{eq:dyadic-cost-sum-bound}
\end{equation}
The same argument for general \(q\), now using
\(\sum_{g\mid q}g^{-1}\le1+\log q\), also gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal C(q)\le q\{9+8(1+\log q)^3\}.
 \label{eq:general-cost-sum-bound}
\end{equation}

Exact Euclidean-algorithm enumeration through \(a=25\) gives
\[
 \gamma_2^{(25)}
 =\frac13\sum_{a=1}^{25}3^{-a}\mathcal C(2^a)
 =\frac{13180988392373}{2541865828329}.
\]
Using \(\log2<7/10\) in \eqref{eq:dyadic-cost-sum-bound}, the remaining
geometric quadratic sum is rational and satisfies
\[
 \begin{split}
 0\le\gamma_2-\gamma_2^{(25)}
 &\le\frac13\sum_{a=26}^{\infty}
  \left(\frac23\right)^a
  \left\{\frac{17}{2}+16\left(1+\frac{7a}{20}\right)^2\right\}\\
 &=\frac{126600871936}{2541865828329}.
 \end{split}
\]
Thus
\[
 \gamma_2\le\frac{4435863088103}{847288609443},
\]
which, with outward rounding of \(\log2\), proves
\eqref{eq:dyadic-speed-certificate}.

It remains to certify \(v_c\).  Put
\[
 R(s):=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
 \qquad
 H:=-R'(\sigma_0),
 \qquad
 D:=\sum_{q\ge2}\mathcal C(q)q^{-\sigma_0}.
\]
Then \eqref{main-eq:critical-pressure-slopes} gives \(v_c=H/D\).  For completeness,
the interval computation uses, for \(s>1\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 Z_8(s)={}&\sum_{n=1}^{31}n^{-s}
 +\frac{32^{1-s}}{s-1}+\frac12 32^{-s}\\
 &+\sum_{k=1}^{8}\frac{B_{2k}}{(2k)!}
       (s)_{2k-1}32^{1-s-2k}.
 \end{split}
\]
The periodic-Bernoulli remainder and its differentiated form give
\begin{align*}
 |\zeta(s)-Z_8(s)|
 &\le\frac{|B_{16}|}{16!}(s)_{15}32^{-s-15},\\
 |\zeta'(s)-Z_8'(s)|
 &\le\frac{|B_{16}|}{16!}32^{-s-15}\\
 &\quad{}\times\left\{
  \frac{(s)_{16}'}{s+15}
  +(s)_{16}\left(\frac{\log32}{s+15}
                  +\frac1{(s+15)^2}\right)
 \right\}.
\end{align*}
Directed interval evaluation gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 R(2.4787)-2&\in
 [0.000131507893202250,0.000131507893202251],\\
 R(2.4788)-2&\in
 [-0.000127411416688770,-0.000127411416688769].
 \end{split}
\]
Since \(R\) is strictly decreasing,
\(\sigma_0\in[2.4787,2.4788]\).  Moreover,
\(-R'(s)=\sum_{q\ge2}\phi_{\rm E}(q)(\log q)q^{-s}\) is strictly decreasing.
The same interval calculation at the two endpoints gives the outward
certificate
\begin{equation}
 H\in[2.588435643856306896,2.589951928201414596].
 \label{eq:H-interval-certificate}
\end{equation}

Exact integer enumeration of \(\mathcal C(q)\) for \(2\le q\le20000\), with
only the powers \(q^{-s}\) evaluated by directed rounding, gives
\[
 \sum_{q=2}^{20000}\mathcal C(q)q^{-\sigma_0}
 \in[19.302273469878911856,19.311145544445741772].
\]
For the lower tail, fix \(1\le p\le7900\).  The elementary continued-fraction
identities for the symmetric residues imply, for \(q>20000\),
\[
 c(p/q)+c((q-p)/q)\ge\frac{4q}{p}-6.
\]
Indeed, \(p/q<1/2\), and replacing the initial partial quotient \(a_1\)
by \(1,a_1-1\) shows that \(S(p/q)=S((q-p)/q)\).  If \(p>1\), the first
Euclidean quotient is \(\lfloor q/p\rfloor\) and the remaining quotient sum
is at least \(2\); for \(p=1\), the quotient sum is \(q\).  These observations
give the displayed inequality (in fact, with room to spare).
The function
\(g_{p,s}(x)=4x^{1-s}/p-6x^{-s}\) is decreasing in the relevant range,
because
\[
 \frac{3(2.4787)(7900)}{2(2.4787-1)}<19864<20000.
\]
Every block of \(p\) consecutive integers contains exactly
\(\phi_{\rm E}(p)\) integers coprime to \(p\).  The selected residue pairs
are disjoint, and blockwise integration therefore gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{q>20000}\mathcal C(q)q^{-\sigma_0}
 &\ge\sum_{p=1}^{7900}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(p)}p
 \bigg\{\frac{4(20000+p)^{2-\sigma_0}}
                 {p(\sigma_0-2)}\\
 &\hspace{43mm}
 -\frac{6(20000+p)^{1-\sigma_0}}{\sigma_0-1}\bigg\}\\
 &\ge0.434421763138508560.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The integrand is positive and decreases as \(s\) increases, so the final
outward evaluation is made at \(s=2.4788\).
For the opposite direction, \eqref{eq:general-cost-sum-bound} and the
integral test yield, with
\(f_s(x)=x^{1-s}\{9+8(1+\log x)^3\}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{q>20000}\mathcal C(q)q^{-\sigma_0}
 &\le f_{2.4787}(20000)
       +\int_{20000}^{\infty}f_{2.4787}(x)\,dx\\
 &\le347.686170804099215772.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here direct differentiation shows that \(f_s\) is decreasing for
\(s\ge2.4787\) and \(x\ge20000\); the largest upper integrand occurs at
\(s=2.4787\).
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 D\in[19.736695233017420416,366.997316348544957544].
 \label{eq:D-interval-certificate}
\end{equation}
Equations \eqref{eq:H-interval-certificate} and
\eqref{eq:D-interval-certificate} prove
\eqref{eq:critical-speed-certificate}; subtraction gives
\eqref{eq:strict-speed-separation}.  All integer enumerations, analytic
remainders, and rounding directions in this certificate are reproduced by
the accompanying script \texttt{verify\_speed\_separation.py}.

Finally, \(\alpha<v_c<v_2\) implies
\[
 \frac{m}{r_m}\longrightarrow\frac{\log2}{\alpha}>\gamma_2.
\]
The finite-window assertion of \Cref{thm:dyadic-exact-multiplier} applies and
gives \eqref{eq:dyadic-uniform-speed-counterexample}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Polynomial conditional upper tail]
\label{prop:conditional-polynomial-upper-tail}
Under the fixed-window hypotheses of
\Cref{thm:conditional-phase-separation}, there exist \(\delta>0\) and
\(c>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(m\),
\[
 \Pr\left\{
  \frac1mL(g_m(\mathbf X_{m,\alpha,\varepsilon}))
  -\frac{\alpha+\varepsilon}{v_c}>\delta
 \right\}
 \ge c m^{1-\sigma_0}.
\]
In particular, this upper deviation has exponential decay rate zero.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Retain \(b=\alpha+\varepsilon\) and \(r=1/v_c\), so that \(rb<1\).
Fix \(h>0\), and let \(Z_m\) denote the cardinality of the conditioning set.
Choose
\[
 0<\theta_0<\theta_1<\frac{1-rb}{2}
\]
and then \(\zeta>0\) sufficiently small that
\((r+\zeta)b+2\theta_1<1\) and
\(2\theta_0-\zeta b>0\).  For
\(\theta_0m\le q\le\theta_1m\), consider critical renewal words with
\[
 bm-\log q-2h<T\le bm-\log q-h,
 \qquad |S/T-r|\le\zeta.
\]
Equations \eqref{eq:blackwell-critical-renewal} and
\eqref{eq:marked-renewal-reward-law}, uniformly in this tail family of
intervals, show that their unweighted number is at least
\[
 c_0e^{\sigma_0bm}q^{-\sigma_0}
\]
for a fixed \(c_0>0\).  Append to each word the letter \(1/q\).  The free-word
decomposition makes all resulting words distinct, while
\[
 c(1/q)=2q-1,
 \qquad H(1/q)=\log q.
\]
Their total energies lie in \((bm-2h,bm-h]\).  By the choices of
\(\theta_1\) and \(\zeta\), their total costs are at most \(m-1\) for large
\(m\), so \(K_m=4\); by the choices of \(\theta_0\) and \(\zeta\), their
costs divided by \(m\) exceed \(rb\) by a fixed positive amount.
Consequently the exceptional-state count is at least
\[
 c_1e^{\sigma_0bm}
 \sum_{\theta_0m\le q\le\theta_1m}q^{-\sigma_0}
 \ge c_2e^{\sigma_0bm}m^{1-\sigma_0}.
\]
On the other hand, covering the whole conditioning interval by intervals of
length \(h\), using \(K_m\le4\) and the deterministic bound \(N_h\), gives
\(Z_m\le c_3e^{\sigma_0bm}\).  Division proves the asserted lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{abstract}
Let \(R(n)\) be the number of partitions of \(n\) into distinct Fibonacci
numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Sidorov--Vershik's finite
representation frequencies are the same subset-sum coefficients after the
shift from their convention \(F^{\rm SV}_j=F_{j+1}\).  Their normalized
frequencies approximate the Erd\H{o}s measure.  Consequently the layer moment
pressure is the affine normalization
\(P(t)=t\log2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi\) of the \(L^q\)-spectrum of the
golden-ratio Bernoulli convolution.  Lau--Ngai determined the positive-\(q\)
spectrum, while Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and
its negative first-order phase transition.  We record the exact dictionary
and recover those results in Fibonacci-partition coordinates.  The arithmetic
  refinements identify the critical parameter by
  \(\zeta(\sigma_0-1)/\zeta(\sigma_0)=2\).  A one-large-partial-quotient
  theorem proves the local denominator-layer law
  \(b_{2d+1}(s)\sim2\{\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)\}^2d^{-s}\) for every fixed
  \(s>2\).  At criticality its explicit context constant is \(b_C=8\); the
  resulting stable-renewal expansion gives the first noninteger correction of
  order \(m^{3-\sigma_0}\) to the one-layer and finite-window partition sums.
  The critical Gibbs law converges to a uniform mixture of generating-layer
  fractions.  Under the
 uniform law on \(\mathcal I_m\), \(m^{-1}\log R(n)\) satisfies a full large
 deviation principle; the rate is affine on the coexistence interval.  Jointly
 with normalized generating cost, it satisfies a two-dimensional large
 deviation principle whose rate surface has an explicit affine coexistence
face.  The inputs specific to these refinements are a weighted renewal identity
for Weinstein's free generators and a parity-free orbit-filling argument for
the nonexposed slopes.

A finite-window Zeckendorf fold provides an exact finite model for the same
spectrum: its fiber list is the list of \(R\) on two consecutive layers.
An affine permutation also identifies each fiber with a finite Fibonacci
subset-sum coefficient and a partition-function difference.  This yields the
 exact largest fibers
 \(D_{2k}=F_{k+2}\) for \(k\ge0\), \(D_{2k+1}=2F_{k+1}\) for \(k\ge1\), and
 \(D_m=D_{m-2}+D_{m-4}\) for \(m\ge6\), including every maximizing residue.  The two-layer
model has the same pressure and large-deviation rate, an exact frozen
Dirichlet limit, and a critical finite-size constant \(4/\mu_C\).  On every
fixed finite prime support we retain an exact rational coefficient generating
function; no directional coefficient asymptotic is asserted.
\end{abstract}

\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic denominator-layer theorem]
\label{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
For a finite word \(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\) of positive integers, let
\(\mathcal K(\mathbf a)\) be its regular continuant, with
\[
 \begin{gathered}
  \mathcal K(\varnothing)=1,\qquad \mathcal K(a_1)=a_1,\\
  \mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)
  =a_r\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1})
   +\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-2}).
 \end{gathered}
\]
Put
\[
 \begin{aligned}
  \mathcal C_{\rm L}&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
   \bigcup_{r\ge1}\mathbb N^r,\\
  \mathcal C_{\rm R}&:=\{\varnothing\}\cup
   \{(a_1,\ldots,a_r):r\ge1,\ a_i\ge1,\ a_r\ge2\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Then, for every fixed \(s>2\),
\begin{equation}
 b_{2d+1}(s)\sim b(s)d^{-s}\qquad(d\to\infty),
 \label{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}
\end{equation}
where the constant is the absolutely convergent one-large-partial-quotient
context sum
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 b(s)
 &: =\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
       \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}
       \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\\
 &=2\left(\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}\right)^2>0.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}
\end{equation}
In particular, this identifies the polynomial scale of every fixed
low-temperature denominator layer; no tail hypothesis is used in
\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write \(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\), with
\(|\varnothing|_1=0\).  The canonical regular continued fraction of a reduced
\(p/q\in(0,1)\) is
\[
 \frac pq=[0;a_1,\ldots,a_r],
 \qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_r\ge2,
\]
and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\).  The conversion formula
used in the proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} gives
\[
 d(p/q)=|\mathbf a|_1-1.
\]
Consequently, on putting \(n=d+1\), the left side of
\eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer} is
\begin{equation}
 A_n(s):=
 \sum_{\substack{\mathbf a\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\|\mathbf a|_1=n}}
 \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-s}.
 \label{eq:regular-continuant-layer}
\end{equation}

We first evaluate the context mass.  Canonical words in
\(\mathcal C_{\rm R}\) with
denominator \(q\) parameterize the \(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in
\((0,1)\).  Hence, for \(s>2\),
\begin{equation}
 R_s:=\sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}\mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s}
 =1+\sum_{q\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(q)}{q^s}
 =\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}<\infty.
 \label{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}
\end{equation}
Every nonempty positive word either ends in a digit at least two or has the
form \((a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)\).  The usual terminal move
\[
 (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1},1)
 \longleftrightarrow
 (a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1}+1)
\]
preserves the continuant.  It pairs the two regular expansions of every
nonempty canonical word; it also pairs \((1)\) with \(\varnothing\).  Therefore
\begin{equation}
 L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}\mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
 =2R_s.
 \label{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}
\end{equation}
This proves the absolute convergence and the evaluation in
\eqref{eq:one-large-partial-quotient-context-sum}.

It remains to prove that this context sum is the whole local main term.  We
give the cutoff argument, including the multiple-large-digit and moderate
parts.  The continuant concatenation formula implies, for finite positive
words \(\mathbf u,\mathbf v\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal K(\mathbf u\mathbf v)
 \ge \mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v).
 \label{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound}
\end{equation}
Moreover, with the two contexts fixed and \(a\to\infty\), multilinearity of
the tridiagonal determinant defining the continuant gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)
 =a\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)+O_{\mathbf u,\mathbf v}(1).
 \label{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine}
\end{equation}

Let \(P_n(s)\) be the part of \eqref{eq:regular-continuant-layer} coming from
words having a digit greater than \(n/2\).  Such a digit is unique.  Cutting
there is a bijection with pairs
\((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\times\mathcal C_{\rm R}\)
satisfying
\(|\mathbf u|_1+|\mathbf v|_1<n/2\), the middle digit being
\(a=n-|\mathbf u|_1-|\mathbf v|_1\).  Equations
\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} and
\eqref{eq:continuant-large-digit-affine} give, respectively,
\[
 n^s\mathcal K(\mathbf u,a,\mathbf v)^{-s}
 \le 2^s\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}
\]
and pointwise convergence of the left side to
\(\{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-s}\).  Dominated
convergence, using \eqref{eq:right-continuant-context-mass}--
\eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, therefore yields
\begin{equation}
 n^sP_n(s)\longrightarrow L_sR_s=b(s).
 \label{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}
\end{equation}

We now show that the complementary words have total weight \(o(n^{-s})\).
Choose
\begin{equation}
 \frac{s}{2(s-1)}<\delta<1,
 \qquad h=\lfloor n^\delta\rfloor,
 \label{eq:large-digit-cutoff}
\end{equation}
and set
\[
 \eta_s(h):=
 \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
 \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
\]
By \eqref{eq:left-continuant-context-mass}, \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).  A word having
at least two digits not smaller than \(h\) can be cut at its first two such
digits.  After dropping the restrictions on the three intervening contexts,
\eqref{eq:continuant-concatenation-lower-bound} bounds its total weight by
\begin{equation}
 L_s^2R_s
 \left(\sum_{a\ge h}a^{-s}\right)^2
 =O_s(h^{2-2s})=o(n^{-s}),
 \label{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}
\end{equation}
where the last equality is precisely the first inequality in
\eqref{eq:large-digit-cutoff}.

For completeness, consider a word all of whose digits are smaller than
\(h\).  Greedily divide it into consecutive blocks: close a block as soon as
its digit sum reaches \(h\), and leave the last remainder unclosed.  Every
closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum at least
\(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.  The
concatenation bound and the uniqueness of the greedy decomposition show that
the total continuant weight of all such words is at most
\begin{equation}
 \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
 \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1}
 \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large \(h\).  When \(N\ge n/4\), this is
\(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A>0\), because \(n/h\to\infty\) and
\(\eta_s(h)\to0\).

The words not counted by \(P_n(s)\) and not covered by
\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible} have at most one digit at least \(h\).
If there is none, apply \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} with \(N=n\).  If
there is exactly one, its value is at most \(n/2\), so the two surrounding
moderate contexts have combined digit sum at least \(n/2\); one has digit sum
at least \(n/4\).  Cutting at the exceptional digit, summing its weight
\(a^{-s}\), and applying \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound} to that long context
again gives \(o(n^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A\).  Together with
\eqref{eq:two-large-digits-negligible}, this proves
\[
 A_n(s)-P_n(s)=o(n^{-s}).
\]
Combining this with \eqref{eq:principal-large-digit-limit}, and replacing
\(n=d+1\) by \(d\), proves \eqref{eq:low-temperature-local-layer}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic critical stable renewal]
\label{thm:arithmetic-critical-stable-renewal}
Put \(\alpha:=\sigma_0-1\in(1,2)\), and under the critical letter law put
\[
 \Pr\{(C,H)=(c(p/q),\log q)\}=q^{-\sigma_0}.
\]
Then \(\Pr\{C=2d+1\}=b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)\), and the explicit constants
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 b_C&:=
 \sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
 \sum_{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}}
 \{\mathcal K(\mathbf u)\mathcal K(\mathbf v)\}^{-\sigma_0}
 =2\left(\frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}\right)^2=8,\\
 K_C&:=\frac{2^{\sigma_0-1}}{\sigma_0-1}b_C
 =\frac{2^{\sigma_0+2}}{\sigma_0-1}
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:critical-tail-constants}
\end{equation}
are positive.  The double series defining \(b_C\) is absolutely convergent,
and
\begin{align}
 b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)&\sim b_Cd^{-\sigma_0},
 &&d\to\infty,
 \label{eq:critical-letter-local-tail}\\
 \Pr\{C>x\}
 &=\sum_{q\ge2}q^{-\sigma_0}
   \card{\{1\le p<q:(p,q)=1,\ c(p/q)>x\}},\notag\\
 &\sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0},
 &&x\to\infty.
 \label{eq:critical-letter-tail}
\end{align}
If \(u_j=u_j(\sigma_0)\) is the renewal sequence in
\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-coefficients}, then
\begin{equation}
 u_j=\frac1{\mu_C}
 +\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)}j^{2-\sigma_0}
 +o(j^{2-\sigma_0}).
 \label{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{align}
 Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)
 &=\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
 +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
 \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order}\\
 S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
 &=\frac{4m}{\mu_C}
 +\frac{4K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}
   m^{3-\sigma_0}+o(m^{3-\sigma_0}).
 \label{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}
\end{align}
Finally, \(C\) belongs to the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive
\(\alpha\)-stable law.  More precisely, if \(a_n>0\) is chosen so that
\(n\Pr\{C>a_n\}\to1\), then for independent copies \(C_1,C_2,\ldots\),
\begin{equation}
 \frac{C_1+\cdots+C_n-n\mu_C}{a_n}
 \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\mathcal S_\alpha,
 \label{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal S_\alpha\) is the spectrally positive \(\alpha\)-stable law
whose L\'evy measure has density \(\alpha x^{-\alpha-1}\) on \((0,\infty)\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The critical equation \eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} makes the displayed
letter law a probability measure.  The local estimate
\eqref{eq:critical-letter-local-tail} and the context-sum evaluation in
\eqref{eq:critical-tail-constants} are \Cref{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer}
at \(s=\sigma_0\).  Direct summation of that local estimate gives
\[
 \Pr\{C>x\}
 =\sum_{d>(x-1)/2}b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)
 \sim\frac{b_C}{\sigma_0-1}
      \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^{1-\sigma_0},
\]
which is \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail} with the stated \(K_C\).  Thus
regular variation is a conclusion of the arithmetic continuant estimate, not
an assumption.

The distribution of \(C\) has span one, finite mean \(\mu_C\), and tail
\(K_Cj^{-\alpha}\), with \(1<\alpha<2\).  The finite-mean case of the
discrete renewal-sequence theorem \cite{OmeyVanGulck2015} applies.  To make
its constant explicit, write \(\overline F(j)=\Pr\{C>j\}\).  The tail-sum
identity and the Abelian theorem for power series give, as \(z\uparrow1\),
\begin{align*}
 1-B_{\sigma_0}(z)
 &=(1-z)\sum_{j\ge0}\overline F(j)z^j,\\
 \sum_{j\ge0}\overline F(j)z^j
 &=\mu_C+K_C\Gamma(1-\alpha)(1-z)^{\alpha-1}
   +o((1-z)^{\alpha-1}).
\end{align*}
Since \(U_{\sigma_0}(z)=\{1-B_{\sigma_0}(z)\}^{-1}\), it follows that
\[
 U_{\sigma_0}(z)
 =\frac1{\mu_C(1-z)}
 -\frac{K_C\Gamma(1-\alpha)}{\mu_C^2}(1-z)^{\alpha-2}
 +o((1-z)^{\alpha-2}).
\]
The cited arithmetic coefficient theorem, using the span-one hypothesis,
transfers this expansion locally.  As
\(\Gamma(2-\alpha)=(1-\alpha)\Gamma(1-\alpha)\), it gives
\[
 u_j-\frac1{\mu_C}
 \sim\frac{K_C}{\mu_C^2(\alpha-1)}j^{1-\alpha};
\]
see also the generating-function remainder argument for the arithmetic
renewal theorem in \cite[Ch.~XI]{Feller1971}.  Substitution of
\(\alpha=\sigma_0-1\) proves
\eqref{eq:critical-renewal-second-order}.  Summing it and using
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^{m-1}j^{2-\sigma_0}
 \sim\frac{m^{3-\sigma_0}}{3-\sigma_0}
\]
in the exact identities \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} and
\eqref{eq:weighted-window-renewal} proves
\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-second-order} and
\eqref{eq:finite-window-critical-second-order}; the boundary terms are
\(O(1)=o(m^{3-\sigma_0})\).

Finally, \eqref{eq:critical-letter-tail}, finite mean, and the absence of a
negative tail are precisely the one-sided domain-of-attraction conditions for
an \(\alpha\)-stable law with the normalization in
\eqref{eq:critical-cost-stable-domain}; see \cite[Ch.~XVII]{Feller1971}.
\end{proof}

 succeeded in 212ms:
\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

On the standard Fibonacci layer
\(\mathcal I_m=[F_{m+1}-1,F_{m+2}-1)\), the classical partition function
\(R\) has a pressure \(P\) that is exactly the affine normalization
\(P(t)=t\log2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi\) of the known golden-ratio Bernoulli
convolution spectrum.  The all-real spectrum and its first-order transition
are due to Lau--Ngai, Feng--Olivier, and Feng
\cite{LauNgai1998,FengOlivier2003,Feng2005}.  In the renewal coordinates of
this paper one obtains the exact frozen limit
\[
 \sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^{-s}
 \longrightarrow\frac2{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-1
 \qquad(s>\sigma_0),
\]
 and the critical leading law \(2m/\mu_C\).  The arithmetic denominator-layer
 theorem sharpens this to
 \[
  \sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^{-\sigma_0}
  =\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
  +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}m^{3-\sigma_0}
  +o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
 \]
 where \(b_C=8\) is an explicit absolutely convergent continuant context sum
 and \(K_C=2^{\sigma_0-1}b_C/(\sigma_0-1)\).  Its critical Gibbs measure
has the coexistence limit \((v_cU,U)\), and its uniform logarithmic
multiplicity satisfies the full LDP with the affine rate
\(\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha\) on \([0,v_c]\).  These are one-layer theorems
about the standard partition function, not consequences inferred from a
two-layer mixture.

The finite-window fiber spectrum provides an exact finite model and admits
two descriptions.  The affine
permutation \(\pi_m\) identifies each multiplicity with a coefficient of a
finite Fibonacci subset-sum polynomial and with a Fibonacci-lag difference of
the indexed partition function.  The interval identity identifies the same
fiber list with ordinary partition values on two consecutive Fibonacci
layers.  The latter correspondence transfers the published extremal
classification, after an explicit convention change, and yields
\[
 D_{2k}=F_{k+2},\qquad D_{2k+1}=2F_{k+1},\qquad
 D_m=D_{m-2}+D_{m-4}\quad(m\ge6),
\]
together with the complete maximizing-residue list.

For negative real tilts, Weinstein's orbit counts recover the known frozen
half-line and evaluate its critical point arithmetically:
\[
 P(t)=0\qquad(t\le-\sigma_0),
 \qquad
 \frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}=2.
\]
The uniform layer-count lemma treats the two unit conventions, the levels
\(1\) and \(2\), shared endpoints, and early layers explicitly.
At the unnormalized scale, however, the local spectrum stabilizes exactly and
\[
 S_{-s}(m)\longrightarrow
 \frac4{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-2
 \qquad(s>\sigma_0).
\]
This function has a simple pole at \(\sigma_0\), produces an explicit
total-variation Gibbs limit, and yields the Tauberian law
\(\sum_{k\le x}\Psi(k)\sim
x^{\sigma_0}/(\sigma_0\kappa)\).  A separate Jensen lower bound proves
positive lower exponential growth for \(t>-\beta_*\), where
  \(\beta_*=2.2705594539\ldots\).  The weighted free-generator renewal equation,
together with the published Stern--Brocot denominator pressure, gives an
independent derivation in the present finite-layer coordinates of
\[
 \{t:P(t)>0\}=(-\sigma_0,\infty).
\]
The analyticity, strict convexity, and derivative corner on the positive
phase agree with Feng's all-real spectrum.  The renewal coordinates give the
finite positive continued-fraction formula for the right derivative, while
the frozen branch gives the zero left derivative.
At the critical tilt itself, the arithmetic local law and the exact renewal
identity give
\[
 S_{-\sigma_0}(m)
 =\frac{4m}{\mu_C}
 +\frac{4K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}m^{3-\sigma_0}
 +o(m^{3-\sigma_0}).
\]
The input is the proved estimate
\(b_{2d+1}(\sigma_0)\sim8d^{-\sigma_0}\), not an assumed regular-variation
hypothesis.  Its one-large-partial-quotient proof controls two large digits
and the all-moderate regime separately, so the local mass has no residual
lattice or semistable oscillation.
The associated finite-window Gibbs measure has a nondegenerate coexistence
limit: the generating-layer fraction is uniform on \([0,1]\), and the
normalized log multiplicity is its product with \(v_c\).

The derivative jump prevents the G\"artner--Ellis theorem alone from treating
the intervening slopes.  A finite-window orbit-filling construction supplies
their matching local lower bounds and proves a full large deviation principle;
its good rate function is affine on the coexistence interval.

On a standard Fibonacci layer, retaining normalized generator cost together
with normalized log multiplicity yields a full two-dimensional large
deviation principle.  Its rate is the perspective of the scalar rate, and its
coexistence region is the affine face
\(J(\beta,\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha\) for
\(0\le\alpha\le\beta v_c\).  The lower bound combines fixed-cost exponential
tilting with an exact low-reward cost filler.

The exact finite-prime-support generating function isolates a remaining
arithmetic boundary.  Its cost-summed coefficients are rational, but the
marked cost has infinite second moment already on the dyadic ray and has no
positive exponential moment.  A directional coefficient law would require
both a parameter-uniform multivariate smooth-point theorem and uniform tail
control for that unbounded cost.  Neither is proved here, so no directional
quenched velocity or active-cutoff asymptotic for \(C_m(k)\) is claimed.

Conditional arithmetic and integer-moment consequences are collected in the
separately compiled supplement.  No transducer-based collision kernel,
algebraicity statement for \(\lambda_q\), arithmetic-window recurrence
polynomial, exact-kernel certificate, Galois group, or Chebotarev density is
claimed in the main article or supplement.
