\section{Visible entropy rates and canonical bands}\label{sec:ledger}

Since \(p_m(x)=d_m(x)/2^m\), the visible law under uniform input is the
\(q=1\) canonical ensemble.  With the all-\(q\) asymptotics of \(S_q(m)\) in
hand, we obtain its integer-order R\'enyi entropy rates
\cite{CoverThomas2006} and sharp exponential tail estimates.

\begin{definition}[Visible law under uniform input]
\label{def:visible-law}
For \(m\ge0\), the visible law is the probability measure on \(X_m\) obtained
by pushing the uniform law on \(\Omega_m\) forward by \(\Fold_m\):
\[
  p_m(x):=2^{-m}\card{\{\omega\in\Omega_m:\Fold_m(\omega)=x\}}
  =
  \frac{d_m(x)}{2^m}
  \qquad (x\in X_m).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Typical visible thickness band]
\label{cor:visible-band}
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), let
\[
  B_m(\varepsilon):=
  \left\{
    x\in X_m:
    \Delta_1-\varepsilon\le \frac1m\log d_m(x)
    \le \Delta_2+\varepsilon
  \right\}.
\]
Then
\[
  p_m(B_m(\varepsilon))
  \ge 1-\exp\!\bigl(-(\varepsilon+o(1))m\bigr).
\]
Here \(\Delta_1=\log2-\log\varphi\), because
\(S_1(m)=2^m\) and \(S_0(m)=F_{m+2}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:visible-law},
\[
  p_m(x)=\frac{d_m(x)}{S_1(m)}=\mu_{m,1}(x).
\]
Apply \Cref{thm:gibbs-selection} with \(q=1\).  The two exceptional tails
outside the displayed band each have mass at most
\(\exp(-(\varepsilon+o(1))m)\), and the sum of two such errors is still
\(\exp(-(\varepsilon+o(1))m)\), giving the displayed lower bound for the
band mass.  Finally,
\[
  \Delta_1=P_1-P_0=\log2-\log\varphi,
\]
using \(P_1=\log\lambda_1=\log2\) from \(S_1(m)=2^m\) and
\(P_0=\log\varphi\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Integer-order R\'enyi entropy rates]
\label{thm:renyi-entropy-rate}
\leanverified{paper_projection_renyi_entropy_rate}
For every integer \(q\ge2\), let
\[
  H_q(p_m):=\frac{1}{1-q}\log\sum_{x\in X_m}p_m(x)^q
\]
be the R\'enyi entropy of order \(q\).  Then the entropy rate
\[
  h_q:=\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1mH_q(p_m)
\]
exists and is
\[
  h_q=\frac{q\log2-P_q}{q-1}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
  \lim_{q\to\infty}h_q=\log2-\frac12\log\varphi .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:visible-law},
\[
  \sum_{x\in X_m}p_m(x)^q
  =
  2^{-mq}\sum_{x\in X_m}d_m(x)^q
  =
  2^{-mq}S_q(m).
\]
Therefore
\[
  H_q(p_m)
  =
  \frac{1}{1-q}\bigl(\log S_q(m)-mq\log2\bigr)
  =
  \frac{mq\log2-\log S_q(m)}{q-1}.
\]
For fixed \(q\ge2\), \Cref{thm:all-q-transfer} gives
\[
  \frac1m\log S_q(m)\to P_q,
\]
so the displayed rate follows.  Finally,
\[
  h_q
  =
  \frac{q}{q-1}\log2-\frac{q}{q-1}\cdot\frac{P_q}{q}.
\]
By \Cref{cor:renyi-endpoint}, \(P_q/q=\log(\lambda_q^{1/q})\to
\frac12\log\varphi\), and hence \(h_q\to
\log2-\frac12\log\varphi\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Visible-tail envelope for thick fibers]
\label{cor:visible-thick-tail}
\leanverified{paper_projection_visible_thick_tail}
For \(\alpha\ge0\), set
\[
  E_m(\alpha):=
  \left\{x\in X_m:\frac1m\log d_m(x)\ge\alpha\right\}.
\]
Then, for every integer \(q\ge1\),
\[
  \limsup_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log p_m(E_m(\alpha))
  \le
  P_q-\log2-(q-1)\alpha .
\]
Consequently,
\[
  \limsup_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log p_m(E_m(\alpha))
  \le
  \inf_{q\ge1}\bigl(P_q-\log2-(q-1)\alpha\bigr).
\]
If \(\alpha>\frac12\log\varphi\), then \(p_m(E_m(\alpha))=0\) for all
sufficiently large \(m\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
On \(E_m(\alpha)\), the inequality \(d_m(x)\ge e^{\alpha m}\) gives
\[
  d_m(x)\le e^{-(q-1)\alpha m}d_m(x)^q
  \qquad(q\ge1).
\]
Thus
\[
  p_m(E_m(\alpha))
  =
  2^{-m}\sum_{x\in E_m(\alpha)}d_m(x)
  \le
  2^{-m}e^{-(q-1)\alpha m}S_q(m).
\]
Taking logarithms, dividing by \(m\), and applying
\Cref{thm:all-q-transfer} gives the first bound.  Taking the infimum over
\(q\ge1\) gives the second.  The final assertion follows from
\Cref{thm:max-fiber}: if \(\alpha>\frac12\log\varphi\), then eventually
\(D_m<e^{\alpha m}\), so \(E_m(\alpha)=\varnothing\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Collision entropy rate]
\label{thm:collision-entropy-rate}
\leanverified{paper_projection_collision_entropy_rate}
The collision entropy
\[
  H_2(p_m):=-\log\sum_{x\in X_m}p_m(x)^2
\]
satisfies
\[
  \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1mH_2(p_m)=2\log2-P_2.
\]
Equivalently, \(H_2(p_m)=h_2m+o(m)\) with
\[
  h_2=2\log2-\log\lambda_2.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
This is \Cref{thm:renyi-entropy-rate} with \(q=2\).  Explicitly,
\[
  \sum_{x\in X_m}p_m(x)^2=2^{-2m}S_2(m),
\]
so
\[
  H_2(p_m)=2m\log2-\log S_2(m).
\]
Since \(m^{-1}\log S_2(m)\to P_2=\log\lambda_2\), the asserted rate follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[R\'enyi-2 asymptotics]
\label{cor:renyi2}
Let \(p(\lambda)=\lambda^3-2\lambda^2-2\lambda+2\), and let
\(\lambda_-\in(-2,-1)\), \(\lambda_+\in(0,1)\), and \(\rho\in(2,3)\) be its
three real roots.  With the constants
\[
  T_2(m)=c_\rho\rho^m+c_-\lambda_-^m+c_+\lambda_+^m
\]
from \Cref{thm:q2-alternating-second-order}, one has
\[
  \sum_{x\in X_m}p_m(x)^2
  =
  4^{-m}\bigl(c_\rho\rho^m+c_-\lambda_-^m+c_+\lambda_+^m\bigr),
\]
where \(c_\rho>0\) and \(c_-\ne0\).  In particular,
\[
  \begin{aligned}
  H_2(p_m)
  &=
  m(2\log2-\log\rho)-\log c_\rho\\
  &\quad{}
  -\log\!\left(
    1+\frac{c_-}{c_\rho}\left(\frac{\lambda_-}{\rho}\right)^m
      +\frac{c_+}{c_\rho}\left(\frac{\lambda_+}{\rho}\right)^m
  \right),
  \end{aligned}
\]
and the leading rate is \(2\log2-\log\rho=2\log2-P_2\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:T2}, \(T_2(m)=S_2(m)\).  The exact expansion of \(T_2(m)\) is
\Cref{thm:q2-alternating-second-order}; substituting it into
\[
  \sum_{x\in X_m}p_m(x)^2=4^{-m}S_2(m)
\]
gives the first display.  Since \(\rho\) is the unique dominant root and
\(c_\rho>0\), factor \(c_\rho\rho^m\) out of \(S_2(m)\) and take minus the
logarithm.  This gives the displayed formula for \(H_2(p_m)\).
\Cref{rem:chow-jones} identifies the dominant root \(\rho\) with
\(\lambda_2\), so \(\log\rho=P_2\).
\end{proof}

standard character-orthogonality formula.  The finite-window contributions in
\Cref{sec:residue-affine} are the explicit reversal--complement bijection and
affine residue permutation of \Cref{thm:affine-transfer}, together with the
pointwise fiber formula in \Cref{thm:partition-difference}; the latter follows
by truncating the indexed Fibonacci partition generating function.  The
two-interval fiber identity in \Cref{thm:fiber-partition-interval} is also
specific to the finite-window fold.

The values and maximizing residues in
\Cref{thm:unconditional-extremal-fibers} are not a new extremal classification:
they are the exact convention-and-interval transfer of Theorems~4.7 and~5.3 of
Koc\'abov\'a, Mas\'akov\'a, and Pelantov\'a
\cite{KocabovaMasakovaPelantova2005};
\Cref{cor:extremal-fiber-recurrence} is then an immediate Fibonacci-recurrence
consequence.  The additional ingredient in the negative-tilt argument is the
uniform early-layer estimate proved from Weinstein's orbit formulas.  That
estimate, which strengthens eventual layer stabilization to a bound valid in
every layer, yields \Cref{prop:negative-temperature-freezing}.  The local
microcanonical limit and the exact unnormalized
partition function in \Cref{sec:local-spectrum} combine this finite-window
two-layer identity with Weinstein's published orbit decomposition.  The
Wiener--Ikehara theorem itself is classical \cite{Korevaar2004};
\Cref{thm:psi-tauberian} is its application to the specific orbit Dirichlet
series, and \Cref{thm:pressure-transition-strip} is a separate finite-window
Jensen and maximum-level estimate.  Weinstein's free-monoid bijection,
multiplier multiplicativity, orbit decomposition, and largest-index formula
are published
  \cite[Prop.~3.3 and Thms.~3.8, 5.1, and 10.3]{Weinstein2016}; none of
  these mechanisms is claimed here.  The Stern--Brocot/Knauf denominator
  pressure is likewise published.  The weighted length renewal in
  \Cref{prop:weighted-generator-renewal} and its exact finite-window transfer
  are additional steps here; the resulting pressure is the
  Bernoulli-convolution spectrum under \eqref{eq:erdos-pressure-dictionary},
  not a new pressure theorem.  The local denominator-layer theorem
  \Cref{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer} is a separate arithmetic result; its
  proof does not assume the regular variation later used by the renewal
  transfer.
The one-layer pressure, critical Gibbs law, and LDP in
\Cref{thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics} are consequences for the
standard function \(R\) itself.  Their lower-bound proof uses the one-layer
orbit weights directly and does not infer componentwise behavior from the
two-layer fiber mixture.
The standard large-deviation upper bound and the lower bounds at exposed
slopes are separated in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp} from the new finite-window
orbit-filling argument, which supplies the missing lower bounds at the
nonexposed coexistence slopes.
The marked critical renewal identity is a bivariate restatement of
\Cref{prop:weighted-generator-renewal}, whereas its conditional consequences
are additional finite-window results.  The arithmetic renewal theorem and
Blackwell's renewal theorem are classical inputs and are not reproved; the
stable second-order coefficients and uniform coexistence law are their
finite-window transfers through the exact boundary identities after the
critical cost tail has been proved arithmetically.

The separately compiled supplement keeps the conditional arithmetic and
integer-moment consequences outside the main theorem spine.  It labels the
moment constants as transfers of Sanna's theorem and the governing quadratic
cubic as already present in work of Chow and Jones \cite{ChowJones2024}.

\subsection{Related work}

The uniqueness theorem underlying the legal expansion is due to Zeckendorf
\cite{Zeckendorf1972}; Lekkerkerker's work provides classical background on
the same numeration system \cite{Lekkerkerker1952}.  Berstel developed the
normalization and automata viewpoint for Fibonacci representations
\cite{Berstel2001}.  The representation-counting function itself has been
studied through recurrence formulas, partition identities, extremal bounds,
and automata by Carlitz \cite{Carlitz1968}, Robbins \cite{Robbins1996},
Bicknell-Johnson and Fielder \cite{BicknellJohnsonFielder1999}, Stockmeyer
\cite{Stockmeyer2008}, Chow and Slattery \cite{ChowSlattery2021}, and Shallit
\cite{Shallit2021}.  Weinstein's orbit and level-set analysis
\cite{Weinstein2016} and the exact extremal classification of Koc\'abov\'a,
Mas\'akov\'a, and Pelantov\'a \cite{KocabovaMasakovaPelantova2005} are the
specific inputs to \Cref{sec:extremal-ldp}.  Sanna proved the power-sum
asymptotics used here and the endpoint law
\(\lim_{q\to\infty}\lambda_q^{1/q}=\varphi^{1/2}\)
\cite[Thms.~1.1 and~1.2]{Sanna2025}.  Zhou gives a broader treatment of
representation functions for related numeration systems and, in particular,
resolves the logarithmic-average conjecture of Chow and Slattery
\cite[Cor.~1.5]{Zhou2023}.
Chow and Jones obtained the same cubic that appears in the quadratic
finite-window recurrence in their analysis of the variance of the partition
function \cite{ChowJones2024}.
The probabilistic version of these finite counts is the Erd\H{o}s measure:
Sidorov and Vershik identify its level masses as normalized Fibonacci
representation frequencies \cite{SidorovVershik1998}.  Hu's local-dimension
analysis \cite{Hu1997}, Lau and Ngai's exact positive-\(q\) spectrum
\cite{LauNgai1998}, Feng and Olivier's weak-Gibbs phase-transition theorem
\cite{FengOlivier2003}, and Feng's explicit all-real golden-ratio formula
\cite{Feng2005} are the direct priority line for the pressure in this paper.
The Stern--Brocot pressure and its Knauf-model realization are taken from
Kesseb\"ohmer--Stratmann and Fiala--Kleban--\"Ozl\"uk
\cite{KessebohmerStratmann2007,FialaKlebanOzluk2003}.  The earlier
Stern--Brocot multifractal theorem of Kesseb\"ohmer and Stratmann
\cite{KessebohmerStratmann2004} concerns interval growth rates, rather than
Fibonacci partition multiplicities or the finite-window uniform law.  The
critical continued-fraction moment uses the fixed-denominator mean theorem of Panov and
Liehl, as recorded in the quantitative modern treatment of
Aistleitner--Borda--Hauke
\cite{Panov1982,Liehl1983,AistleitnerBordaHauke2023}.

\subsection{Organization}

\Cref{sec:preliminaries} defines the finite-window fold and fixes notation.
\Cref{sec:residue-affine} proves the residue, affine, and partition-difference
formulas.  \Cref{sec:extremal-ldp} proves the interval identity, transfers the
extremal classification, records the finite-layer recovery of the frozen
branch, and isolates the large-deviation interface at the pressure corner.
\Cref{sec:local-spectrum} proves local spectral stabilization, the exact
unnormalized partition function and Gibbs law, the orbit-count Tauberian
asymptotic, the pressure dictionary and arithmetic critical refinements, and
the full large deviation principle across the pressure corner.
\Cref{sec:standard-thermodynamics} proves the one-layer pressure, critical
law, scalar LDP, and joint generation-cost/multiplicity LDP for the classical
Fibonacci partition function itself.
The separately compiled supplement
contains conditional arithmetic refinements, the dyadic ray, and the integer
moment transfer.

 succeeded in 278ms:
\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Let \(F_0=0\), \(F_1=F_2=1\), and
\(F_{j+2}=F_{j+1}+F_j\), and put
\(\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\).  Let \(R(n)\) be the classical Fibonacci
partition function: the number of partitions of \(n\) into distinct
Fibonacci numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  Our main
thermodynamic results concern \(R\) on the standard layers
\[
 \mathcal I_m=[F_{m+1}-1,F_{m+2}-1).
\]
The moment pressure for every real tilt and its first-order transition are
already contained, under an affine normalization, in the golden-ratio
Bernoulli-convolution literature \cite{LauNgai1998,FengOlivier2003,Feng2005}.
We make that normalization explicit and use it as the starting point for
finite-window identities, arithmetic critical refinements, and full
large-deviation lower bounds for \(m^{-1}\log R(n)\) under the uniform law on
\(\mathcal I_m\).

A finite-window Zeckendorf fold gives an exact finite model for this standard
object.  A word
\(\omega\in\{0,1\}^m\) determines the raw sum
\[
  N_m(\omega)=\sum_{j=1}^m\omega_jF_{j+1}.
\]
We consider the finite-window fold obtained by reducing this sum modulo
\(F_{m+2}\) and taking the unique legal Zeckendorf word in the visible
window.  If \(d_m(x)\) is the cardinality of the fiber over a legal word
\(x\), the corresponding finite problem is to identify the multiset
\(\{d_m(x):x\in X_m\}\) and its extremal and moment statistics.

The bridge is exact: the complete fiber list is the list of \(R\) on
\(\mathcal I_m\sqcup\mathcal I_{m+1}\).  A second correspondence is an affine
reindexing of a finite subset-sum spectrum.  Both are finite identities and
do not require a normalization transducer.

\subsection{Main results}

Put \(R(n)=0\) for \(n<0\).  Let \(\sigma_0>2\) be the unique solution of
\[
 \frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}=2;
 \qquad \sigma_0=2.4787507857\ldots.
\]
For \(t>-\sigma_0\), let \(P(t)>0\) be the unique solution of
\[
 \sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
 q^t e^{-P(t)c(p/q)}=1,
\]
where \(c(p/q)\) is the odd continued-fraction cost defined before
\Cref{prop:weighted-generator-renewal}, and put \(P(t)=0\) for
\(t\le-\sigma_0\).  Set
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \mu_C:=\sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
 c(p/q)q^{-\sigma_0},\\
 v_c:=\frac{\displaystyle
 \sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
 q^{-\sigma_0}\log q}{\mu_C},
 \qquad
 t_c:=-\sigma_0,\qquad
 \alpha_+:=\frac12\log\varphi.
 \end{gathered}
\]
Define
\[
 Z_m^R(t):=\sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^t.
\]

The arithmetic input at the critical point is a local theorem, rather than a
tail assumption.  For every fixed \(s>2\),
\begin{equation}
 b_{2d+1}(s)
 \sim2\left(\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}\right)^2d^{-s}.
 \label{eq:introduction-low-temperature-layer}
\end{equation}
Its proof cuts a canonical regular continued fraction at its unique large
partial quotient and gives the constant as an absolutely convergent left--right
continuant context sum.  At \(s=\sigma_0\), this constant is \(b_C=8\), and
\begin{equation}
 \Pr\{C>x\}\sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0},
 \qquad K_C=\frac{2^{\sigma_0-1}}{\sigma_0-1}b_C.
 \label{eq:introduction-critical-cost-tail}
\end{equation}
Consequently, \Cref{thm:arithmetic-critical-stable-renewal} proves
\begin{equation}
 Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)
 =\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
 +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}m^{3-\sigma_0}
 +o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
 \label{eq:introduction-standard-critical-second-order}
\end{equation}
with the corresponding coefficient doubled for \(S_{-\sigma_0}(m)\).  The
critical cost also lies in the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive
\((\sigma_0-1)\)-stable law.  Regular variation in these statements is derived
from \eqref{eq:introduction-low-temperature-layer}; it is not assumed.

\begin{theoremA}[One-layer Fibonacci partition thermodynamics]
For every \(t\in\RR\),
\[
 \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log Z_m^R(t)=P(t).
\]
For \(s>\sigma_0\),
\[
 Z_m^R(-s)\longrightarrow
 \frac2{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-1,
\]
whereas \(Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)\sim2m/\mu_C\).  Under the critical Gibbs law
proportional to \(R(n)^{-\sigma_0}\), the normalized log multiplicity and
generating-layer cost converge jointly to \((v_cU,U)\), with \(U\) uniform on
\([0,1]\).

If \(\mathbf N_m\) is uniform on \(\mathcal I_m\), then
\(m^{-1}\log R(\mathbf N_m)\) satisfies a full large deviation principle
with good rate function
\[
 I(\alpha)=\sup_{t\in\RR}\{t\alpha-P(t)+\log\varphi\}.
\]
Its effective domain is \([0,\alpha_+]\), and
\(I(\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha\) on \([0,v_c]\).
\end{theoremA}

This is \Cref{thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics}.  Its pressure assertion
is the Lau--Ngai/Feng spectrum under
\eqref{eq:erdos-pressure-dictionary}; it is included to normalize the critical
finite-size law and the uniform-layer LDP.  The latter statements use the
one-layer orbit weights \(2,1\), rather than a deduction from the two-layer
fiber mixture.

The same renewal representation retains the normalized generating cost
\(B_m^R=m^{-1}\ell_m^R(\mathbf N_m)\).
\Cref{thm:joint-cost-reward-ldp} proves a full LDP for
\((B_m^R,Y_m^R)\).  Its rate is
\[
 J(\beta,\alpha)=
 (1-\beta)\log\varphi+\beta I(\alpha/\beta)
 \quad(0<\beta\le1,\ 0\le\alpha\le\beta\alpha_+),
\]
with \(J(0,0)=\log\varphi\) and \(J=+\infty\) elsewhere.  In particular,
\[
 J(\beta,\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
 \qquad(0\le\alpha\le\beta v_c),
\]
so coexistence is an affine face of the joint rate surface rather than an
artifact of one-dimensional projection.  Fixed-cost exponential tilting
supplies the strictly convex part; an exact one- or two-letter low-reward
suffix fills every sufficiently large remaining cost on the affine face.

For the exact finite-window model, put
\(R^\dagger(n)=R(n)+R(n-1)\).  Let
\[
  \widetilde d_m(n)=[z^n]\prod_{j=1}^m(1+z^{F_j}),
  \qquad 0\le n<F_{m+2}.
\]
For residues modulo \(F_{m+2}\), define
\[
  \pi_m(n)\equiv F_{m+1}n+F_{m+1}-1\pmod{F_{m+2}}.
\]

\begin{theoremB}[Affine fiber--partition correspondence]
For every \(m\ge1\), the map \(\pi_m\) is a permutation and
\[
  d_m^\#(\pi_m(n))
  =\widetilde d_m(n)
  =R^\dagger(n)-R^\dagger(n-F_{m+1})
  \qquad(0\le n<F_{m+2}).
\]
\end{theoremB}

This combines \Cref{thm:affine-transfer,thm:partition-difference}.  It gives a
pointwise correspondence, not only an equality of aggregate moments.

There is also a direct interval description:
\[
 d_m^\#(r)=
 \begin{cases}
 R(F_{m+2}+r),&0\le r\le F_{m+1}-2,\\
 R(r),&F_{m+1}-1\le r<F_{m+2}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The known extremal classification of Koc\'abov\'a, Mas\'akov\'a, and

 succeeded in 279ms:
Pelantov\'a can therefore be transferred exactly after an explicit change of
Fibonacci convention.

\begin{theoremC}[Interval identity and largest fibers]
Let \(D_m=\max_{x\in X_m}d_m(x)\).  Then
\[
 D_0=D_1=1,\qquad D_{2k}=F_{k+2}\ (k\ge0),\qquad
 D_{2k+1}=2F_{k+1}\ (k\ge1),
\]
and \(D_m=D_{m-2}+D_{m-4}\) for every \(m\ge6\).  The maximizing residues,
including the exceptional initial cases, are given in
\Cref{thm:unconditional-extremal-fibers}.
\end{theoremC}

For a real tilt \(t\), put
\[
  S_t(m)=\sum_{x\in X_m}d_m(x)^t.
\]
The identity
\[
  \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log S_t(m)=0
  \qquad(t\le-\sigma_0)
\]
is recorded in \Cref{prop:negative-temperature-freezing} as a finite-layer
recovery of the frozen branch proved by Feng--Olivier and Feng
\cite{FengOlivier2003,Feng2005}.  The renewal coordinates evaluate the
boundary arithmetically and supply the finite-size consequences below.

The fixed-level information is sharper than the exponential pressure.  Put
\(C_m(k)=\card{\{x\in X_m:d_m(x)=k\}}\), and let \(\Psi(k)\) be Weinstein's
number of generating orbits at level \(k\).

\begin{theoremE}[Local spectrum and critical Gibbs law]
For \(m\ge1\), \(C_m(1)=2\), while for \(k\ge2\),
\[
 C_m(k)\le4\Psi(k),
 \qquad C_m(k)=4\Psi(k)\quad(m\ge2k).
\]
For every \(s>\sigma_0\),
\[
 S_{-s}(m)\longrightarrow
 \mathcal Z(s):=\frac4{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-2.
\]
This is the exact convergence range for the unnormalized sums.  The function
\(\mathcal Z\) has a simple pole at \(\sigma_0\), and the corresponding
fiber-level Gibbs measures converge in total variation with explicit
critical logarithmic moments.
At the endpoint itself,
\[
 S_{-\sigma_0}(m)\sim\frac{4m}{\mu_C}.
\]
Under the finite-window Gibbs law proportional to
\(d_m(x)^{-\sigma_0}\), the normalized pair consisting of log multiplicity
and generating-layer cost converges in distribution to
\((v_cU,U)\), where \(U\) is uniform on \([0,1]\).
\end{theoremE}

The complete statements are
\Cref{thm:local-fiber-spectrum,thm:spectral-partition-function,thm:critical-gibbs-spectrum,thm:critical-finite-window-gibbs}.
They separate an unnormalized critical phenomenon inside the region where
the exponential pressure vanishes.

\begin{theoremF}[Orbit growth and arithmetic critical refinements]
With
\[
 \kappa=-\left.\frac{d}{ds}\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}
 \right|_{s=\sigma_0},
\]
one has
\[
 \sum_{k\le x}\Psi(k)\sim
 \frac{x^{\sigma_0}}{\sigma_0\kappa}.
\]
Moreover, if
\(\beta_*=\log\varphi/\log(2/\varphi)=2.2705594539\ldots\), then
\[
 \liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log S_t(m)>0
 \qquad(t>-\beta_*).
\]
At the known critical point \(t_c=-\sigma_0\), the renewal equation becomes
\[
 \sum_{q\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(q)}{q^{\sigma_0}}=1,
 \qquad
 \frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}=2,
\]
and the positive-phase one-sided derivative is the explicitly convergent
ratio
\[
 P'_+(t_c)=
 \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{q\ge2}\phi_{\rm E}(q)q^{-\sigma_0}\log q}
      {\displaystyle\sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
       c(p/q)q^{-\sigma_0}}.
\]
\end{theoremF}

The all-real existence, implicit branch, frozen phase, and derivative corner
come from Feng's spectrum theorem \cite[Thm.~1.3]{Feng2005} and the
Erd\H{o}s-measure phase transition of Feng--Olivier
\cite[Thms.~2.9--2.10 and App.~A]{FengOlivier2003}.  The theorem above retains
only the Tauberian orbit law, the totient evaluation of the critical equation,
and the one-sided critical moment in the present renewal coordinates.

Let \(\mathbf X_m\) be uniformly distributed on \(X_m\), and put
\[
 Y_m=m^{-1}\log d_m(\mathbf X_m).
\]

\begin{theoremG}[Full large deviations across the freezing corner]
The sequence \((Y_m)\) satisfies a large deviation principle with speed
\(m\) and good rate function
\[
 I(\alpha)=\sup_{t\in\RR}\{t\alpha-P(t)+\log\varphi\}.
\]
Its effective domain is \([0,\alpha_+]\), and
\[
 I(\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
 \qquad(0\le\alpha\le v_c).
\]
For every \(0<\alpha<v_c\), the probabilities of shrinking neighborhoods
have the exact exponential rate \(-I(\alpha)\).
\end{theoremG}

The complete statement and proof are given in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp}.
The new orbit-filling step fills both parities of every sufficiently large
target layer while preserving the source multiplicity.

For a fixed finite set of primes, \Cref{prop:prime-support-interface} gives
the exact joint generating function for multiplier exponents and generator
cost and transfers it to \(C_m(k)\) with the active boundary weights
\(4,3,1\).  We do not assert a directional coefficient or quenched-velocity
asymptotic: the needed parameter-uniform smooth-point estimate and uniform
integrability for the unbounded cost are not supplied by the cited ACSV
results.  \Cref{rem:prime-support-local-open-interface} records the exact
remaining analytic input.

The proof of \Cref{prop:negative-temperature-freezing} includes a separate
layer-count lemma transferring Weinstein's convention \(f_j=F_{j+1}\).  It
distinguishes the levels \(k=1,2\), endpoints, early layers, and the eventual
equality asserted in Weinstein's theorem.

The pressure corner prevents a direct full application of the
G\"artner--Ellis theorem: its lower-bound conclusion does not cover slopes
strictly between the one-sided derivatives at \(-\sigma_0\).  The
orbit-filling argument in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp} supplies those missing
local lower bounds and proves the full large deviation principle, with an
affine rate on the coexistence interval.

\subsection{Contribution boundary}

For auditability, the dependency boundary is summarized before the detailed
discussion.
\noindent\textbf{Koc\'abov\'a--Mas\'akov\'a--Pelantov\'a.}
Imported: extremal values and maximizing integers for the ordinary Fibonacci
partition function.  Proved here from that input: exact convention and
interval transfer to all maximizing finite-window residues.

\noindent\textbf{Weinstein.}
Imported: the free generator monoid, multiplier product, orbit decomposition,
and eventual layer stabilization.  Proved here from that input: the uniform
early-layer bound, weighted cost renewal, exact finite-window transfer, and
the prime-support coefficient interface.

\noindent\textbf{Erd\H{o}s measure and Bernoulli convolutions.}
Sidorov--Vershik use Fibonacci numbers
\(F^{\rm SV}_1=1,F^{\rm SV}_2=2\), hence
\(F^{\rm SV}_j=F_{j+1}\) in our convention.  Their level-\(m\) frequency is
therefore exactly
\begin{align*}
 f_m^{\rm SV}(k)
 &=\#\left\{\boldsymbol\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^m:
   \sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_jF_j^{\rm SV}=k\right\}\\
 &=[z^k]\prod_{j=1}^m(1+z^{F_{j+1}})\\
 &=\#\{\omega\in\{0,1\}^m:N_m(\omega)=k\}.
\end{align*}
Thus the difference is the index shift \(F_j^{\rm SV}=F_{j+1}\), not a
different counting object.  They identify \(2^{-m}f_m^{\rm SV}(k)\) with the
finite masses approximating the Erd\H{o}s measure
\cite[Sec.~3]{SidorovVershik1998}.  Hu studied its golden-ratio local dimensions
\cite{Hu1997}; Lau--Ngai gave the exact \(L^q\)-spectrum for \(q>0\)
\cite{LauNgai1998}; Feng--Olivier and Feng gave the complete real spectrum and
the negative first-order transition \cite{FengOlivier2003,Feng2005}.  These
are imported results, not merely related background.

If \(\mu\) denotes the golden-ratio Bernoulli convolution and
\(\tau_\mu(t)\) uses the convention
\(\tau_\mu(t)=\lim \log\sum_I\mu(I)^t/\log|I|\), then the level masses are
\(2^{-m}\) times the finite Fibonacci representation counts.  Since the net
scale is \(\varphi^{-m}\), the exact exponential-rate dictionary is
\begin{equation}
 P(t)=t\log2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi.
 \label{eq:erdos-pressure-dictionary}
\end{equation}
Thus the all-real pressure, its positive implicit branch, the negative frozen
branch, the first-order corner, and the generic Legendre multifractal
description are prior results.  The present paper adds the exact
  finite-window/fiber correspondences, evaluates Feng's implicit critical
  condition as \(\zeta(\sigma_0-1)/\zeta(\sigma_0)=2\), proves the local
  low-temperature denominator-layer law with its explicit continuant context
  constant, obtains the stable second-order critical terms and uniform
  coexistence law, and proves the stated finite-layer nonexposed-slope lower
  bounds.

The original source confirms the referee’s localization. Dushistova’s Theorem 3 defines \(\mathcal A_n\) with positive digits, final digit at least \(2\), fixed digit sum \(n\), and weight \(K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}\), exactly matching the manuscript after \(s=2\beta\) and \(n=d+1\). In the proof of her Lemma 7 (printed pp. 668–669), the split says it separates \(u=1\), then replaces \(u>1\) by twice a canonical convolution; that replacement includes the empty canonical prefix, while the \(u=0\) case is not separately retained. This produces the excess \(R_s\), so the discrepancy is a narrow endpoint bookkeeping error, not a convention mismatch.

\ifdefined\supplementonly

The remaining transition strip admits an exact renewal description.  For a
reduced fraction \(p/q\in(0,1)\), write its unique negative continued fraction
as
\[
 \frac pq=
 \cfrac1{a_1-\cfrac1{a_2-\ddots-\cfrac1{a_r}}},
 \qquad a_i\ge2,
\]
and set
\[
 d(p/q):=\sum_{i=1}^r(a_i-1),
 \qquad c(p/q):=2d(p/q)+1.
\]
For a finite vector \(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\), define its negative
continuant by
\[
 \begin{gathered}
  \mathcal D(\varnothing)=1,\qquad \mathcal D(a_1)=a_1,\\
  \mathcal D(a_1,\ldots,a_r)
  =a_r\mathcal D(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-1})
   -\mathcal D(a_1,\ldots,a_{r-2}).
 \end{gathered}
\]
Thus the denominator of the displayed negative continued fraction is
\(\mathcal D(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\).

For real \(s\), put
\begin{equation}
 b_\ell(s):=
 \sum_{\substack{0<p<q,\ (p,q)=1\\c(p/q)=\ell}}q^{-s},
 \qquad
 u_0(s):=1,\qquad
 u_j(s):=\sum_{\ell=1}^j b_\ell(s)u_{j-\ell}(s).
 \label{eq:weighted-renewal-coefficients}
\end{equation}
Every sum defining \(b_\ell(s)\) is finite.  More explicitly,
\begin{equation}
 b_{2d+1}(s)
 =\sum_{r=1}^d
   \sum_{\substack{e_1+\cdots+e_r=d\\e_i\ge1}}
   \mathcal D(e_1+1,\ldots,e_r+1)^{-s},
 \qquad b_{2d}(s)=0.
 \label{eq:weighted-letter-coefficients}
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}[Weighted generator renewal]
\label{prop:weighted-generator-renewal}
For \(j\ge1\), let
\[
 \Lambda_j(s):=\sum_{n\in\mathcal I_j}R(n)^{-s}.
\]
Then, for every real \(s\),
\begin{equation}
 \Lambda_j(s)
 =1+u_j(s)+2\sum_{\ell=1}^{j-1}u_\ell(s)
 =2\sum_{\ell=0}^{j-1}u_\ell(s)+u_j(s)-1.
 \label{eq:weighted-layer-renewal}
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every \(m\ge1\),
\begin{equation}
 S_{-s}(m)
 =4\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_j(s)+3u_m(s)+u_{m+1}(s)-2.
 \label{eq:weighted-window-renewal}
\end{equation}
Moreover, with formal power series
\[
 B_s(z):=\sum_{\ell\ge1}b_\ell(s)z^\ell,
 \qquad U_s(z):=\sum_{j\ge0}u_j(s)z^j,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 U_s(z)=\frac1{1-B_s(z)}.
 \label{eq:weighted-renewal-generating-function}
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We use the generating-number parameterization in
\cite[Secs.~3--4]{Weinstein2016}, but not its layer-stabilization theorem.
Under Weinstein's free-monoid bijection, a generating number \(g\) corresponds
uniquely to a nonempty word
\[
 w=\frac{p_1}{q_1}\times\cdots\times\frac{p_r}{q_r}
\]
in reduced fractions from \((0,1)\).  Proposition~3.3 and formula~(16) of
that paper give, in the present notation,
\begin{equation}
 R(g)=\prod_{i=1}^r q_i,
 \qquad L(g)=\sum_{i=1}^r c(p_i/q_i).
 \label{eq:generator-weight-length}
\end{equation}
The continued-fraction bijection also gives
\eqref{eq:weighted-letter-coefficients}.  Unique decomposition of a free word
therefore shows that \(u_j(s)\) is exactly the sum of \(R(g)^{-s}\) over all
generating numbers with \(L(g)=j\), and proves
\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-generating-function} as a formal identity.

It remains to count each generating orbit in a fixed layer.  A generating
number belongs to Weinstein's odd first-index sheet, so its initial-block
parameter is \(1\).  The formulas already established in
\eqref{eq:L-a-shift}--\eqref{eq:L-sigma-shift} consequently specialize to
\[
 L([a]g)=L(g)+2a,\qquad
 L([a]\tau g)=L(g)+1+2a,\qquad
 L(\sigma n)=L(n)+1
\]
for \(a\ge0\).  Hence the two branches in Weinstein's first sheet contribute
one point to every layer \(j\ge L(g)\); their sigma images contribute one
further point precisely when \(j>L(g)\).  The action is free and distinct
generating orbits are disjoint.  Since \(\mathcal I_j\) contains exactly one
point of partition multiplicity \(1\) for \(j\ge1\), summing the orbit weights
gives \eqref{eq:weighted-layer-renewal}.  The two-layer identity
\eqref{eq:real-collision-two-layers} then gives
\eqref{eq:weighted-window-renewal}.  Notice that the restriction \(j\ge1\) is
essential in \eqref{eq:weighted-layer-renewal}, because \(\mathcal I_0\) is
empty.
\end{proof}

Let \(\mathfrak P\) denote the Stern--Brocot pressure
\[
 \mathfrak P(\theta)
 :=\lim_{d\to\infty}\frac1d
   \log\sum_{T\in\mathcal T_d}|T|^\theta .
\]
We use the generation convention in which the first interior fraction
\(1/2\) has depth \(d=1\).  The denominator form of the same pressure
\cite[Sec.~2 and Thm.~1.1]{KessebohmerStratmann2007} is
\begin{equation}

 \label{eq:stern-brocot-denominator-convention}
\end{equation}

\subsection{Main results}

Put \(R(n)=0\) for \(n<0\).  Let \(\sigma_0>2\) be the unique solution of
\[
 \frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}=2;
 \qquad \sigma_0=2.4787507857\ldots.
\]
For \(t>-\sigma_0\), let \(P(t)>0\) be the unique solution of
\[
 \sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
 q^t e^{-P(t)c(p/q)}=1,
\]
where \(c(p/q)\) is the odd continued-fraction cost defined before
\Cref{prop:weighted-generator-renewal}, and put \(P(t)=0\) for
\(t\le-\sigma_0\).  Set
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \mu_C:=\sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
 c(p/q)q^{-\sigma_0},\\
 v_c:=\frac{\displaystyle
 \sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
 q^{-\sigma_0}\log q}{\mu_C},
 \qquad
 t_c:=-\sigma_0,\qquad
 \alpha_+:=\frac12\log\varphi.
 \end{gathered}
\]
Define
\[
 Z_m^R(t):=\sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^t.
\]

The arithmetic input at the critical point is a local theorem, rather than a
tail assumption.  For every fixed \(s>2\),
\begin{equation}
 b_{2d+1}(s)
 \sim2\left(\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}\right)^2d^{-s}.
 \label{eq:introduction-low-temperature-layer}
\end{equation}
Its proof cuts a canonical regular continued fraction at its unique large
partial quotient and gives the constant as an absolutely convergent left--right
continuant context sum.  At \(s=\sigma_0\), this constant is \(b_C=8\), and
\begin{equation}
 \Pr\{C>x\}\sim K_Cx^{1-\sigma_0},
 \qquad K_C=\frac{2^{\sigma_0-1}}{\sigma_0-1}b_C.
 \label{eq:introduction-critical-cost-tail}
\end{equation}
Consequently, \Cref{thm:arithmetic-critical-stable-renewal} proves
\begin{equation}
 Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)
 =\frac{2m}{\mu_C}
 +\frac{2K_C}{\mu_C^2(\sigma_0-2)(3-\sigma_0)}m^{3-\sigma_0}
 +o(m^{3-\sigma_0}),
 \label{eq:introduction-standard-critical-second-order}
\end{equation}
with the corresponding coefficient doubled for \(S_{-\sigma_0}(m)\).  The
critical cost also lies in the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive
\((\sigma_0-1)\)-stable law.  Regular variation in these statements is derived
from \eqref{eq:introduction-low-temperature-layer}; it is not assumed.

\begin{theoremA}[One-layer Fibonacci partition thermodynamics]
For every \(t\in\RR\),
\[
 \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log Z_m^R(t)=P(t).
\]
For \(s>\sigma_0\),
\[
 Z_m^R(-s)\longrightarrow
 \frac2{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-1,
\]
whereas \(Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)\sim2m/\mu_C\).  Under the critical Gibbs law
proportional to \(R(n)^{-\sigma_0}\), the normalized log multiplicity and
generating-layer cost converge jointly to \((v_cU,U)\), with \(U\) uniform on
\([0,1]\).

If \(\mathbf N_m\) is uniform on \(\mathcal I_m\), then
\(m^{-1}\log R(\mathbf N_m)\) satisfies a full large deviation principle
with good rate function
\[
 I(\alpha)=\sup_{t\in\RR}\{t\alpha-P(t)+\log\varphi\}.
\]
Its effective domain is \([0,\alpha_+]\), and
\(I(\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha\) on \([0,v_c]\).
\end{theoremA}

This is \Cref{thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics}.  Its pressure assertion
is the Lau--Ngai/Feng spectrum under
\eqref{eq:erdos-pressure-dictionary}; it is included to normalize the critical
finite-size law and the uniform-layer LDP.  The latter statements use the
one-layer orbit weights \(2,1\), rather than a deduction from the two-layer
fiber mixture.

The same renewal representation retains the normalized generating cost
\(B_m^R=m^{-1}\ell_m^R(\mathbf N_m)\).
\Cref{thm:joint-cost-reward-ldp} proves a full LDP for
\((B_m^R,Y_m^R)\).  Its rate is
\[
 J(\beta,\alpha)=
 (1-\beta)\log\varphi+\beta I(\alpha/\beta)
 \quad(0<\beta\le1,\ 0\le\alpha\le\beta\alpha_+),
\]
with \(J(0,0)=\log\varphi\) and \(J=+\infty\) elsewhere.  In particular,
\[
 J(\beta,\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
 \qquad(0\le\alpha\le\beta v_c),
\]
so coexistence is an affine face of the joint rate surface rather than an
artifact of one-dimensional projection.  Fixed-cost exponential tilting
supplies the strictly convex part; an exact one- or two-letter low-reward
suffix fills every sufficiently large remaining cost on the affine face.

For the exact finite-window model, put
\(R^\dagger(n)=R(n)+R(n-1)\).  Let
\[
  \widetilde d_m(n)=[z^n]\prod_{j=1}^m(1+z^{F_j}),

\]
For residues modulo \(F_{m+2}\), define
\[
  \pi_m(n)\equiv F_{m+1}n+F_{m+1}-1\pmod{F_{m+2}}.
\]

\noindent\textbf{Erd\H{o}s measure and Bernoulli convolutions.}
Sidorov--Vershik use Fibonacci numbers
\(F^{\rm SV}_1=1,F^{\rm SV}_2=2\), hence
\(F^{\rm SV}_j=F_{j+1}\) in our convention.  Their level-\(m\) frequency is
therefore exactly
\begin{align*}
 f_m^{\rm SV}(k)
 &=\#\left\{\boldsymbol\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^m:
   \sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_jF_j^{\rm SV}=k\right\}\\
 &=[z^k]\prod_{j=1}^m(1+z^{F_{j+1}})\\
 &=\#\{\omega\in\{0,1\}^m:N_m(\omega)=k\}.
\end{align*}
Thus the difference is the index shift \(F_j^{\rm SV}=F_{j+1}\), not a
different counting object.  They identify \(2^{-m}f_m^{\rm SV}(k)\) with the
finite masses approximating the Erd\H{o}s measure
\cite[Sec.~3]{SidorovVershik1998}.  Hu studied its golden-ratio local dimensions
\cite{Hu1997}; Lau--Ngai gave the exact \(L^q\)-spectrum for \(q>0\)
\cite{LauNgai1998}; Feng--Olivier and Feng gave the complete real spectrum and
the negative first-order transition \cite{FengOlivier2003,Feng2005}.  These
are imported results, not merely related background.

If \(\mu\) denotes the golden-ratio Bernoulli convolution and
\(\tau_\mu(t)\) uses the convention
\(\tau_\mu(t)=\lim \log\sum_I\mu(I)^t/\log|I|\), then the level masses are
\(2^{-m}\) times the finite Fibonacci representation counts.  Since the net
scale is \(\varphi^{-m}\), the exact exponential-rate dictionary is
\begin{equation}
 P(t)=t\log2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi.
 \label{eq:erdos-pressure-dictionary}
\end{equation}
Thus the all-real pressure, its positive implicit branch, the negative frozen
branch, the first-order corner, and the generic Legendre multifractal
description are prior results.  The present paper adds the exact
  finite-window/fiber correspondences, evaluates Feng's implicit critical
  condition as \(\zeta(\sigma_0-1)/\zeta(\sigma_0)=2\), proves the local
  low-temperature denominator-layer law with its explicit continuant context
  constant, obtains the stable second-order critical terms and uniform
  coexistence law, and proves the stated finite-layer nonexposed-slope lower
  bounds.

\noindent\textbf{Kesseb\"ohmer--Stratmann; Fiala--Kleban--\"Ozl\"uk.}
Imported: Stern--Brocot/Knauf denominator pressure.  It supplies an alternate
derivation of the already known pressure formula in the renewal coordinates
needed for the finite-size arguments.  The polynomial denominator-layer
asymptotic \eqref{eq:introduction-low-temperature-layer}, including its
explicit context constant and the elimination of multiple-large-digit and
moderate-digit contributions, is proved here and is not a pressure
consequence.

\noindent\textbf{Feller; Wiener--Ikehara; G\"artner--Ellis.}
Imported: classical renewal, Tauberian, and exposed-slope large-deviation
tools.  Proved here from those inputs after the arithmetic tail theorem: the
stable second-order critical finite-size laws, uniform coexistence limit, and
orbit-filling lower bounds at nonexposed slopes.

The residue characterization in \Cref{thm:residue-fibers} is a direct
restatement of the fold definition, and \Cref{thm:fourier-inversion} is the
standard character-orthogonality formula.  The finite-window contributions in
\Cref{sec:residue-affine} are the explicit reversal--complement bijection and
affine residue permutation of \Cref{thm:affine-transfer}, together with the
pointwise fiber formula in \Cref{thm:partition-difference}; the latter follows
by truncating the indexed Fibonacci partition generating function.  The
two-interval fiber identity in \Cref{thm:fiber-partition-interval} is also
specific to the finite-window fold.

The values and maximizing residues in
\Cref{thm:unconditional-extremal-fibers} are not a new extremal classification:
they are the exact convention-and-interval transfer of Theorems~4.7 and~5.3 of
Koc\'abov\'a, Mas\'akov\'a, and Pelantov\'a
\cite{KocabovaMasakovaPelantova2005};
\Cref{cor:extremal-fiber-recurrence} is then an immediate Fibonacci-recurrence
consequence.  The additional ingredient in the negative-tilt argument is the
uniform early-layer estimate proved from Weinstein's orbit formulas.  That
estimate, which strengthens eventual layer stabilization to a bound valid in
every layer, yields \Cref{prop:negative-temperature-freezing}.  The local
microcanonical limit and the exact unnormalized
partition function in \Cref{sec:local-spectrum} combine this finite-window
two-layer identity with Weinstein's published orbit decomposition.  The
Wiener--Ikehara theorem itself is classical \cite{Korevaar2004};
\Cref{thm:psi-tauberian} is its application to the specific orbit Dirichlet
series, and \Cref{thm:pressure-transition-strip} is a separate finite-window
Jensen and maximum-level estimate.  Weinstein's free-monoid bijection,
multiplier multiplicativity, orbit decomposition, and largest-index formula
are published
  \cite[Prop.~3.3 and Thms.~3.8, 5.1, and 10.3]{Weinstein2016}; none of
  these mechanisms is claimed here.  The Stern--Brocot/Knauf denominator
  pressure is likewise published.  The weighted length renewal in
  \Cref{prop:weighted-generator-renewal} and its exact finite-window transfer
  are additional steps here; the resulting pressure is the
  Bernoulli-convolution spectrum under \eqref{eq:erdos-pressure-dictionary},
  not a new pressure theorem.  The local denominator-layer theorem
  \Cref{thm:arithmetic-denominator-layer} is a separate arithmetic result; its
  proof does not assume the regular variation later used by the renewal
  transfer.
The one-layer pressure, critical Gibbs law, and LDP in
\Cref{thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics} are consequences for the
standard function \(R\) itself.  Their lower-bound proof uses the one-layer
orbit weights directly and does not infer componentwise behavior from the
two-layer fiber mixture.
The standard large-deviation upper bound and the lower bounds at exposed
slopes are separated in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp} from the new finite-window
orbit-filling argument, which supplies the missing lower bounds at the
nonexposed coexistence slopes.
The marked critical renewal identity is a bivariate restatement of
\Cref{prop:weighted-generator-renewal}, whereas its conditional consequences
are additional finite-window results.  The arithmetic renewal theorem and
Blackwell's renewal theorem are classical inputs and are not reproved; the
stable second-order coefficients and uniform coexistence law are their
finite-window transfers through the exact boundary identities after the
critical cost tail has been proved arithmetically.

The separately compiled supplement keeps the conditional arithmetic and
integer-moment consequences outside the main theorem spine.  It labels the
moment constants as transfers of Sanna's theorem and the governing quadratic
cubic as already present in work of Chow and Jones \cite{ChowJones2024}.

Intuitive Approximations in Discrete Renewal Theory
               Part 1: regularly varying case

                        Edward Omey & Stefan Van Gulck

            KU Leuven, Faculty of Economics and Business ­ Campus Brussels
                             Warmoesberg 26, 1000 Brussels, Belgium

Abstract

It is usually impossible to find explicit expressions for the renewal sequence.
This paper presents a simple method to approximate the renewal sequence,
which covers many of the known approximations. The paper uses the ideas
of Mitov and Omey (2014).

Keywords: renewal sequence, regular variation, approximations
2000 MSC: 60K05, 60E10, 26A12

The Editors
Journal of Number Theory

Dear Editors,

We submit for your consideration the manuscript "Arithmetic Criticality and
Large Deviations for Fibonacci Partitions and Finite-Window Fibers."

The paper studies the classical Fibonacci partition function R(n) and an exact
finite-window Zeckendorf fold. Its number-theoretic contributions are an
arithmetic evaluation of the critical parameter by
zeta(sigma_0-1)/zeta(sigma_0)=2, a low-temperature denominator-layer theorem
with an explicit one-large-partial-quotient context sum, and the resulting
stable second-order critical laws beyond the leading constants 2/mu_C and
4/mu_C. It also proves uniform coexistence laws, finite-layer large deviations
at the nonexposed slopes, and exact finite-window fiber identities.

The pressure framework is attributed directly to the existing theory of the
Erdos measure and the golden-ratio Bernoulli convolution. Sidorov and Vershik's
finite representation frequencies use F_j^(SV)=F_{j+1} in our convention and
are exactly the raw subset-sum coefficients. Hu studied local dimensions,
Lau and Ngai determined the positive-q L^q-spectrum, and Feng--Olivier and
Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative first-order phase
transition. In our convention the normalization is

    P(t) = t log 2 - tau_mu(t) log phi.

Accordingly, the manuscript records the all-real pressure and frozen branch as
recovery and consistency results. It does not claim them as new. A
theorem-by-theorem table in the introduction separates every imported result,
normalization, and surviving contribution.

The finite identities are stated with their exact domains. The affine
fiber--partition correspondence holds for m >= 1. In the maximizing-residue
formulas, I_{2k+1} is defined for k >= 5, while I_{2k} and J_{2k} are defined
for k >= 7. The manuscript also retains an exact rational generating-function
interface on each fixed finite prime support, but asserts no directional
coefficient or quenched-velocity asymptotic.

The main article is in amsart format. A separately compiled supplement contains
conditional arithmetic and integer-moment consequences. All external inputs,
including the extremal classification of Kocabova--Masakova--Pelantova,
Weinstein's free-generator decomposition, Stern--Brocot denominator pressure,
and standard renewal, Tauberian, and large-deviation theorems, are identified
at their points of use.

Thank you for considering this submission.

Sincerely,
The Authors

# Submission Metadata

## Journal

Journal of Number Theory

## Title

Arithmetic Criticality and Large Deviations for Fibonacci Partitions and
Finite-Window Fibers

## Authors

- Haobo Ma, AELF PTE LTD., Singapore
- Wenlin Zhang, National University of Singapore, Singapore

## 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification

11B39, 05A17, 60F10

## Keywords

Fibonacci partition function; Erdos measure; Bernoulli convolution;
Zeckendorf representation; large deviations

## Summary

The manuscript studies the Fibonacci partition function and an exact
finite-window Zeckendorf fold. It identifies the arithmetic critical parameter
by

\[
\frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}=2,
\]

proves the low-temperature denominator-layer asymptotic with its explicit
one-large-partial-quotient context sum, and derives the critical cost tail and
the second-order \(m^{3-\sigma_0}\) corrections beyond the leading constants
\(2/\mu_C\) and \(4/\mu_C\). It also proves uniform coexistence limits and
finite-layer large deviations at nonexposed slopes, and establishes exact
finite-window fiber identities. On
each fixed finite prime support it retains an exact rational coefficient
generating function. It asserts no directional coefficient asymptotic and no
quenched-velocity asymptotic.

## Relation To Prior Results

Sidorov and Vershik use \(F^{\mathrm{SV}}_1=1\) and
\(F^{\mathrm{SV}}_2=2\), so their indexing is

\[
F^{\mathrm{SV}}_j=F_{j+1}.
\]

Their finite representation frequency \(f_m(k)\) is therefore the same raw
finite Fibonacci subset-sum coefficient used in the manuscript, after this
index shift, and \(2^{-m}f_m(k)\) gives the finite masses approximating the
Erdos measure. Hu treated local dimensions of the golden-ratio Bernoulli
convolution. Lau and Ngai determined its positive-\(q\) \(L^q\)-spectrum.
Feng--Olivier and Feng determined the all-real spectrum and its negative
first-order phase transition.

With

\[
\tau_\mu(t)=\lim\frac{\log\sum_I\mu(I)^t}{\log|I|},
\]

the exact normalization used throughout the submission is

\[
P(t)=t\log 2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi.
\]

Accordingly, the all-real pressure formula and the frozen negative branch are
recorded as attributed recovery and consistency results. The surviving
contributions are the arithmetic evaluation of the critical point, the
one-sided critical moment, the local denominator-layer theorem and explicit
context constant, the stable second-order critical finite-size laws and
coexistence laws, the finite-layer nonexposed-slope lower bounds, and the
exact finite-window correspondences and identities.

## Exact Scope Of Finite Formulas

The affine fiber--partition correspondence and partition-difference formula
hold for every integer \(m\ge 1\). The two-interval fiber identity itself is
stated for \(m\ge 0\).

For the maximizing-residue formulas, write \(G_j=F_{j+1}\). The odd-index
quantity

\[
I_{2k+1}=
\begin{cases}
G_{k+1}G_{k-3}+1,&k\text{ even},\\
G_kG_{k-2}+1,&k\text{ odd}
\end{cases}
\]

is defined only for \(k\ge 5\). The even-index quantities

\[
I_{2k}=
\begin{cases}
G_{k+2}G_{k-5}+G_3+1,&k\text{ even},\\
G_{k+1}G_{k-4}+G_3+1,&k\text{ odd}
\end{cases}
\]

and

\[
J_{2k}=
\begin{cases}
G_{k+1}G_{k-3}+1,&k\text{ even},\\
G_kG_{k-2}+1,&k\text{ odd}
\end{cases}
\]

are defined only for \(k\ge 7\). The exceptional initial maximizing residues
are listed separately in the manuscript and are not obtained by extending
these generic formulas below their stated ranges.

The largest-fiber values have their own ranges:

\[
D_0=D_1=1,\qquad D_{2k}=F_{k+2}\quad(k\ge0),\qquad
D_{2k+1}=2F_{k+1}\quad(k\ge1),
\]

and the recurrence \(D_m=D_{m-2}+D_{m-4}\) holds for \(m\ge6\).

- `main.tex` and its section inputs: main article
- `supplement.tex`: separately compiled supplement
- `sec_references.tex`: manually maintained bibliography; BibTeX is not used

# Arithmetic Criticality and Large Deviations for Fibonacci Partitions and Finite-Window Fibers

This directory contains the main manuscript `Arithmetic Criticality and Large
Deviations for Fibonacci Partitions and Finite-Window Fibers` and a separately
compiled supplement. The submission target is the *Journal of Number Theory*.

## Scope

The finite Fibonacci representation frequencies of Sidorov--Vershik are the
subset-sum coefficients used here after the exact shift
\(F_j^{\mathrm{SV}}=F_{j+1}\). With the convention for the golden-ratio
Bernoulli convolution used in the paper, the pressure dictionary is

\[
P(t)=t\log 2-\tau_\mu(t)\log\varphi.
\]

The positive spectrum is attributed to Lau--Ngai, and the all-real spectrum
and negative first-order phase transition are attributed to Feng--Olivier and
Feng; Hu is cited for the early local-dimension theory. The all-real pressure
and frozen branch are recorded as finite-layer recovery and consistency
results.

The main contribution consists of:

- the exact indexing and normalization dictionary from the golden-ratio
  Bernoulli-convolution \(L^q\)-spectrum to Fibonacci partition layers;
- the arithmetic critical point, critical Gibbs law, and full finite-layer
  LDP on a single standard Fibonacci partition layer;
- the low-temperature denominator-layer asymptotic with an explicit
  one-large-partial-quotient context sum, the critical cost tail, and the
  spectrally positive stable domain of attraction;
- the joint generation-cost and log-multiplicity LDP, including its affine
  two-dimensional coexistence face;
- the residue and affine fiber correspondence;
- the pointwise Fibonacci partition-difference formula;
- the exact two-layer interval identity and transferred extremal theorem;
- the uniform Weinstein layer-count lemma and the finite-layer recovery of the
  known negative-temperature frozen branch;
- the second-order critical finite-size laws, with the noninteger
  (m^{3-\sigma_0}) correction, and the uniform critical coexistence limit;
- the full real-tilt large deviation principle across the freezing corner;
- the exact finite-prime-support coefficient interface and the explicit
  heavy-cost obstruction at the active cutoff.

The conditional microcanonical refinements, exact dyadic ray, integer moment
transfer, direct quadratic recurrence, and high-tilt consequences are in
`supplement.pdf`, not in the main theorem spine.

The fixed finite-prime-support result is an exact rational generating-function
interface only. No directional coefficient asymptotic or quenched-velocity
law is asserted.

The affine fiber--partition correspondence is stated for \(m\ge1\). In the
generic maximizing-residue formulas, \(I_{2k+1}\) is defined for \(k\ge5\),
whereas \(I_{2k}\) and \(J_{2k}\) are defined for \(k\ge7\); exceptional
initial cases are listed separately.


\section{Thermodynamics of the Fibonacci partition function}
\label{sec:standard-thermodynamics}

The renewal identity was derived from Weinstein's standard Fibonacci
partition function before it was transferred to the finite-window fold.  We
now state its one-layer consequences intrinsically.  This removes the bespoke
fold from the probabilistic conclusions.

For \(m\ge1\), recall
\[
 \mathcal I_m=[F_{m+1}-1,F_{m+2}-1)
\]
and define
\[
 Z_m^R(t):=\sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^t
 \qquad(t\in\RR).
\]
If \(\mathbf N_m\) is uniform on \(\mathcal I_m\), put
\[
 Y_m^R:=\frac1m\log R(\mathbf N_m).
\((\beta_j,\alpha_j)\in G\cap\mathcal D\) converging to it; for the upper
edge take \(\alpha_j<\beta_j\alpha_+\), and for \(\beta=1\) take
\(\beta_j<1\).  The local bounds already proved and continuity give the
boundary lower bound after \(j\to\infty\).  Taking the infimum over
\(G\cap\mathcal D\), together with the direct point \((0,0)\), proves the
lower bound for every open set and completes the full LDP.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Related work}

The uniqueness theorem underlying the legal expansion is due to Zeckendorf
\cite{Zeckendorf1972}; Lekkerkerker's work provides classical background on
the same numeration system \cite{Lekkerkerker1952}.  Berstel developed the
normalization and automata viewpoint for Fibonacci representations
\cite{Berstel2001}.  The representation-counting function itself has been
studied through recurrence formulas, partition identities, extremal bounds,
and automata by Carlitz \cite{Carlitz1968}, Robbins \cite{Robbins1996},
Bicknell-Johnson and Fielder \cite{BicknellJohnsonFielder1999}, Stockmeyer
\cite{Stockmeyer2008}, Chow and Slattery \cite{ChowSlattery2021}, and Shallit
\cite{Shallit2021}.  Weinstein's orbit and level-set analysis
\cite{Weinstein2016} and the exact extremal classification of Koc\'abov\'a,
Mas\'akov\'a, and Pelantov\'a \cite{KocabovaMasakovaPelantova2005} are the
specific inputs to \Cref{sec:extremal-ldp}.  Sanna proved the power-sum
asymptotics used here and the endpoint law
\(\lim_{q\to\infty}\lambda_q^{1/q}=\varphi^{1/2}\)
\cite[Thms.~1.1 and~1.2]{Sanna2025}.  Zhou gives a broader treatment of
representation functions for related numeration systems and, in particular,
resolves the logarithmic-average conjecture of Chow and Slattery
\cite[Cor.~1.5]{Zhou2023}.
Chow and Jones obtained the same cubic that appears in the quadratic
finite-window recurrence in their analysis of the variance of the partition
function \cite{ChowJones2024}.
The probabilistic version of these finite counts is the Erd\H{o}s measure:
Sidorov and Vershik identify its level masses as normalized Fibonacci
representation frequencies \cite{SidorovVershik1998}.  Hu's local-dimension
analysis \cite{Hu1997}, Lau and Ngai's exact positive-\(q\) spectrum
\cite{LauNgai1998}, Feng and Olivier's weak-Gibbs phase-transition theorem
\cite{FengOlivier2003}, and Feng's explicit all-real golden-ratio formula
\cite{Feng2005} are the direct priority line for the pressure in this paper.
The Stern--Brocot pressure and its Knauf-model realization are taken from
Kesseb\"ohmer--Stratmann and Fiala--Kleban--\"Ozl\"uk
\cite{KessebohmerStratmann2007,FialaKlebanOzluk2003}.  The earlier
Stern--Brocot multifractal theorem of Kesseb\"ohmer and Stratmann
\cite{KessebohmerStratmann2004} concerns interval growth rates, rather than
Fibonacci partition multiplicities or the finite-window uniform law.  The
critical continued-fraction moment uses the fixed-denominator mean theorem of Panov and
Liehl, as recorded in the quantitative modern treatment of
Aistleitner--Borda--Hauke

 succeeded in 229ms:
The proof of \Cref{prop:negative-temperature-freezing} includes a separate
layer-count lemma transferring Weinstein's convention \(f_j=F_{j+1}\).  It
distinguishes the levels \(k=1,2\), endpoints, early layers, and the eventual
equality asserted in Weinstein's theorem.

The pressure corner prevents a direct full application of the
G\"artner--Ellis theorem: its lower-bound conclusion does not cover slopes
strictly between the one-sided derivatives at \(-\sigma_0\).  The
orbit-filling argument in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp} supplies those missing
local lower bounds and proves the full large deviation principle, with an
affine rate on the coexistence interval.

\subsection{Contribution boundary}

For auditability, the dependency boundary is summarized before the detailed
discussion.
\noindent\textbf{Koc\'abov\'a--Mas\'akov\'a--Pelantov\'a.}
Imported: extremal values and maximizing integers for the ordinary Fibonacci
partition function.  Proved here from that input: exact convention and
interval transfer to all maximizing finite-window residues.

\noindent\textbf{Weinstein.}
Imported: the free generator monoid, multiplier product, orbit decomposition,
and eventual layer stabilization.  Proved here from that input: the uniform
early-layer bound, weighted cost renewal, exact finite-window transfer, and
the prime-support coefficient interface.

\noindent\textbf{Erd\H{o}s measure and Bernoulli convolutions.}
Sidorov--Vershik use Fibonacci numbers
\(F^{\rm SV}_1=1,F^{\rm SV}_2=2\), hence
\(F^{\rm SV}_j=F_{j+1}\) in our convention.  Their level-\(m\) frequency is
therefore exactly
\begin{align*}
 f_m^{\rm SV}(k)
 &=\#\left\{\boldsymbol\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^m:
   \sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_jF_j^{\rm SV}=k\right\}\\
 &=[z^k]\prod_{j=1}^m(1+z^{F_{j+1}})\\
 &=\#\{\omega\in\{0,1\}^m:N_m(\omega)=k\}.
\end{align*}
Thus the difference is the index shift \(F_j^{\rm SV}=F_{j+1}\), not a
different counting object.  They identify \(2^{-m}f_m^{\rm SV}(k)\) with the
finite masses approximating the Erd\H{o}s measure
\cite[Sec.~3]{SidorovVershik1998}.  Hu studied its golden-ratio local dimensions
\cite{Hu1997}; Lau--Ngai gave the exact \(L^q\)-spectrum for \(q>0\)
\cite{LauNgai1998}; Feng--Olivier and Feng gave the complete real spectrum and

 succeeded in 229ms:
fiber-level Gibbs measures converge in total variation with explicit
critical logarithmic moments.
At the endpoint itself,
\[
 S_{-\sigma_0}(m)\sim\frac{4m}{\mu_C}.
\]
Under the finite-window Gibbs law proportional to
\(d_m(x)^{-\sigma_0}\), the normalized pair consisting of log multiplicity
and generating-layer cost converges in distribution to
\((v_cU,U)\), where \(U\) is uniform on \([0,1]\).
\end{theoremE}

The complete statements are
\Cref{thm:local-fiber-spectrum,thm:spectral-partition-function,thm:critical-gibbs-spectrum,thm:critical-finite-window-gibbs}.
They separate an unnormalized critical phenomenon inside the region where
the exponential pressure vanishes.

\begin{theoremF}[Orbit growth and arithmetic critical refinements]
With
\[
 \kappa=-\left.\frac{d}{ds}\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}
 \right|_{s=\sigma_0},
\]
one has
\[
 \sum_{k\le x}\Psi(k)\sim
 \frac{x^{\sigma_0}}{\sigma_0\kappa}.
\]
Moreover, if
\(\beta_*=\log\varphi/\log(2/\varphi)=2.2705594539\ldots\), then
\[
 \liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log S_t(m)>0
 \qquad(t>-\beta_*).
\]
At the known critical point \(t_c=-\sigma_0\), the renewal equation becomes
\[
 \sum_{q\ge2}\frac{\phi_{\rm E}(q)}{q^{\sigma_0}}=1,
 \qquad
 \frac{\zeta(\sigma_0-1)}{\zeta(\sigma_0)}=2,
\]
and the positive-phase one-sided derivative is the explicitly convergent
ratio
\[
 P'_+(t_c)=
 \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{q\ge2}\phi_{\rm E}(q)q^{-\sigma_0}\log q}
      {\displaystyle\sum_{q\ge2}\sum_{\substack{1\le p<q\\(p,q)=1}}
       c(p/q)q^{-\sigma_0}}.
\]
\end{theoremF}

The all-real existence, implicit branch, frozen phase, and derivative corner
come from Feng's spectrum theorem \cite[Thm.~1.3]{Feng2005} and the
Erd\H{o}s-measure phase transition of Feng--Olivier
\cite[Thms.~2.9--2.10 and App.~A]{FengOlivier2003}.  The theorem above retains
only the Tauberian orbit law, the totient evaluation of the critical equation,
and the one-sided critical moment in the present renewal coordinates.

Let \(\mathbf X_m\) be uniformly distributed on \(X_m\), and put
\[
 Y_m=m^{-1}\log d_m(\mathbf X_m).
\]

\begin{theoremG}[Full large deviations across the freezing corner]
The sequence \((Y_m)\) satisfies a large deviation principle with speed
\(m\) and good rate function
\[
 I(\alpha)=\sup_{t\in\RR}\{t\alpha-P(t)+\log\varphi\}.
\]
Its effective domain is \([0,\alpha_+]\), and
\[
 I(\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
 \qquad(0\le\alpha\le v_c).
\]
For every \(0<\alpha<v_c\), the probabilities of shrinking neighborhoods
have the exact exponential rate \(-I(\alpha)\).

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}\{(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ a_1+\cdots+a_r=n\},
+ \qquad
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+
 \begin{proof}
 Write \(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\), with
 \(|\varnothing|_1=0\).  The canonical regular continued fraction of a reduced

+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},

+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}\{(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ a_1+\cdots+a_r=n\},
+ \qquad
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}

-\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic denominator-layer theorem]
+Moshchevitin--Zhigljavsky studied global entropies of Farey-tree partitions
+\cite{MoshchevitinZhigljavsky2004}.  In that line, Dushistova introduced the
+same fixed-digit-sum continuant sum that occurs here and stated a fuller
+asymptotic expansion \cite[Thm.~3]{Dushistova2007}.  Her printed leading
+coefficient, translated to the notation below, is \(R_s+2R_s^2\).  The
+term-by-term identification and the endpoint correction giving \(2R_s^2\)
+are recorded after the theorem statement; the correction concerns the
+leading coefficient in that theorem, not the other results of her paper.
