+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

 The paper studies the classical Fibonacci partition function R(n) and an exact
 finite-window Zeckendorf fold. Its number-theoretic contributions are an
 arithmetic evaluation of the critical parameter by
-zeta(sigma_0-1)/zeta(sigma_0)=2, a low-temperature denominator-layer theorem
-with an explicit one-large-partial-quotient context sum, and the resulting
-stable second-order critical laws beyond the leading constants 2/mu_C and
-4/mu_C. It also proves uniform coexistence laws, finite-layer large deviations
-at the nonexposed slopes, and exact finite-window fiber identities.
+zeta(sigma_0-1)/zeta(sigma_0)=2, a correction and simplified proof of the
+fixed-digit-sum continuant asymptotic, and the resulting stable second-order
+critical laws beyond the leading constants 2/mu_C and 4/mu_C. Following the
+global Farey-tree work of Moshchevitin and Zhigljavsky, Dushistova treated the
+identical local sum and stated a fuller expansion. The manuscript identifies
+the sums term by term and localizes an endpoint bookkeeping error in the proof
+of her Lemma 7: the published leading coefficient R_s+2R_s^2 becomes
+2R_s^2. The correction is restricted to that coefficient; no broader claim
+about her paper is made. The new downstream contribution is the critical
+renewal/Fibonacci transfer. The paper also proves uniform coexistence laws,
+finite-layer large deviations at the nonexposed slopes, and exact
+finite-window fiber identities.
 
 The pressure framework is attributed directly to the existing theory of the
 Erdos measure and the golden-ratio Bernoulli convolution. Sidorov and Vershik's

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

-\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic denominator-layer theorem]
+Moshchevitin--Zhigljavsky studied global entropies of Farey-tree partitions
+\cite{MoshchevitinZhigljavsky2004}.  In that line, Dushistova introduced the
+same fixed-digit-sum continuant sum that occurs here and stated a fuller
+asymptotic expansion \cite[Thm.~3]{Dushistova2007}.  Her printed leading
+coefficient, translated to the notation below, is \(R_s+2R_s^2\).  The
+term-by-term identification and the endpoint correction giving \(2R_s^2\)
+are recorded after the theorem statement; the correction concerns the
+leading coefficient in that theorem, not the other results of her paper.
+
+\begin{theorem}[Corrected denominator-layer asymptotic]

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

-\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic denominator-layer theorem]
+Moshchevitin--Zhigljavsky studied global entropies of Farey-tree partitions
+\cite{MoshchevitinZhigljavsky2004}.  In that line, Dushistova introduced the
+same fixed-digit-sum continuant sum that occurs here and stated a fuller
+asymptotic expansion \cite[Thm.~3]{Dushistova2007}.  Her printed leading
+coefficient, translated to the notation below, is \(R_s+2R_s^2\).  The
+term-by-term identification and the endpoint correction giving \(2R_s^2\)
+are recorded after the theorem statement; the correction concerns the
+leading coefficient in that theorem, not the other results of her paper.

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+
