+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}

+same fixed-digit-sum continuant sum that occurs here and stated a fuller

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

+same fixed-digit-sum continuant sum that occurs here and stated a fuller
+asymptotic expansion \cite[Thm.~3]{Dushistova2007}.  Her printed leading

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

The discrepancy is a narrow endpoint-bookkeeping error in Dushistova’s published proof, not a convention or normalization mismatch.

**Mathematical Resolution**

The evidence is the term-by-term comparison with Dushistova’s Theorem 3 and the specific decomposition in the proof of her Lemma 7, pp. 668–669:

- Dushistova sums over positive regular continued-fraction words \(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\) with \(a_t\ge2\), fixed digit sum \(a_1+\cdots+a_t=n\), and weight \(\mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}\).
- The new Proposition 6.4 proves that the canonical regular-to-negative conversion preserves the represented fraction and denominator and satisfies
  \[
  d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
  \]
  Hence, with \(s=2\beta\) and \(n=d+1\),
  \[
  \boxed{b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)}.
  \]
  The denominator, fixed-sum/cost, final-digit, empty-word, and exponent conventions are all compared explicitly in [sec_arithmetic_critical.tex](/D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_finite_window_zeckendorf_fibers_discrete_thermodynamics_tams/sec_arithmetic_critical.tex:53).
- The two leading coefficients are now displayed side by side:
  \[
  \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2},
  \qquad
  \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2},
  \qquad
  R_s=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}.
  \]
  At \(s=\sigma_0\), these give \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
- The new self-contained endpoint-correction Lemma 6.5 separates the left-context digit sums:
  \[
  u=0:R_s,\qquad u=1:R_s,\qquad u>1:2(R_s-1)R_s.
  \]
  Their sum is
  \[
  R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2.
  \]
- The published proof separates the \(u=1\) contribution and then replaces the \(u>1\) contribution by twice its canonical convolution \(\Sigma_2\). In the displayed definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the \(u>1\) restriction is lost, so the empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\) case is no longer retained separately. The resulting excess is exactly \(R_s\). This localization, including the express disclaimer that it makes no claim about the rest of Dushistova’s paper, is in [sec_arithmetic_critical.tex](/D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_finite_window_zeckendorf_fibers_discrete_thermodynamics_tams/sec_arithmetic_critical.tex:105).

**Priority And Novelty**

Dushistova and Moshchevitin–Zhigljavsky now appear in the abstract, introduction, contribution boundary, contribution table, related-work audit, discussion immediately before Theorem 6.3, supplement discussion, and conclusion. Full bibliographic records and DOIs were added to [sec_references.tex](/D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_finite_window_zeckendorf_fibers_discrete_thermodynamics_tams/sec_references.tex:44) and `references.bib`.

The revised novelty claim is now:

> Dushistova previously treated the identical fixed-digit-sum continuant sum and its polynomial order, and stated a fuller expansion. This paper corrects her printed leading coefficient, gives a shorter context-sum proof of the corrected leading term, derives the critical heavy tail, and transfers it to the renewal/Fibonacci finite-size laws.

The manuscript does not claim priority for the local \(d^{-s}\) order or for Dushistova’s additional expansion coefficients. The settled attribution and recovery wording for Sidorov–Vershik, Lau–Ngai, Feng–Olivier, and Feng remains intact, and the existing recovery propositions remain recovery propositions. The revised contribution boundary and related-work discussion are in [sec_introduction.tex](/D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_finite_window_zeckendorf_fibers_discrete_thermodynamics_tams/sec_introduction.tex:358).

The anti-cheating dependency boundary is preserved. Theorem 6.3 remains a separate arithmetic theorem proved from continued-fraction conversion, finite context sums, continuant inequalities, dominated convergence, and the large/moderate-digit decomposition. It assumes no renewal theorem or regularly varying tail. Regular variation is derived only afterward in Theorem 6.7.

The referee’s proof-completeness repairs were also applied:

- Dominated convergence now has an explicit indicator on the fixed context space and handles the empty right context.
- Lemma 6.6 formalizes the greedy moderate-block factorization, its injection, and the enlargement to arbitrary blocks.
- The exactly-one-large-digit contribution now has the explicit bound
  \[
  2L_s\sum_{h\le a\le n/2}a^{-s}G_s(n/4,h).
  \]
- The oscillation statement is restricted to the leading term and explicitly permits lower-order oscillations.
- The renewal result cites Omey–Van Gulck, Section 3.2, first displayed renewal asymptotic, and verifies nonnegative integer increments, finite mean, regular variation, and span one using costs \(3\) and \(5\).
- The stable-law location convention is fixed by
  \[
  \log\mathbb E e^{it\mathcal S_\alpha}
  =\int_0^\infty(e^{itx}-1-itx)\alpha x^{-\alpha-1}\,dx.
  \]

+\begin{proposition}[Exact identification with Dushistova's sum]
+\label{prop:dushistova-exact-identification}
+For \(n\ge2\) and \(\beta>1\), put
+\(|\mathbf a|_1=a_1+\cdots+a_r\) and use Dushistova's conventions
+\[
+ \mathcal A_n^{\rm D}:=
+ \bigcup_{r\ge1}
+ \{\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb N^r:
+ a_r\ge2,\ |\mathbf a|_1=n\},
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \sigma_\beta(n):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n^{\rm D}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}.
+\]
+Then, term by term,
+\begin{equation}
+ b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)
+ \qquad(d\ge1,\ s>2).
+ \label{eq:dushistova-exact-identification}
+\end{equation}
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Both sides are indexed by reduced fractions in \((0,1)\), but we spell out
+the convention change.  The canonical regular expansion of such a fraction
+is
+\[
+ [0;a_1,\ldots,a_t],\qquad a_i\ge1,\quad a_t\ge2,
+\]
+and its denominator is \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\).  The elementary
+conversion to the unique negative expansion with digits at least two is, for
+even \(t\),
+\[
+ (a_1+1,2^{[a_2-1]},a_3+2,2^{[a_4-1]},\ldots,
+   a_{t-1}+2,2^{[a_t-1]}),
+\]
+where \(2^{[j]}\) denotes a string of \(j\) digits equal to two.  For odd
+\(t>1\), use the same alternating construction through \(a_{t-1}\), followed
+by \(a_t+1\); for \(t=1\), the negative word is \((a_1)\).  Induction in the
+continued-fraction recursions shows that the paired words represent the same
+fraction and hence have the same denominator.  Summing one less than each
+negative digit gives in all three cases
+\[
+ d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
+\]
+Thus \(c(p/q)=2d+1\) is equivalent to
+\((a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in\mathcal A_{d+1}^{\rm D}\), and the summand \(q^{-s}\)
+is exactly \(\mathcal K(a_1,\ldots,a_t)^{-s}\).  Dushistova's exponent is
+\(2\beta\), so \(s=2\beta\), proving the claimed termwise equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Endpoint correction in the left context]
+\label{lem:dushistova-endpoint-correction}
+For \(s>2\), put
+\[
+ r_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf v\in\mathcal C_{\rm R}\\
+                         |\mathbf v|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf v)^{-s},
+ \qquad
+ \ell_m(s):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\
+                            |\mathbf u|_1=m}}
+          \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ r_0=\ell_0=1,\qquad r_1=0,\qquad \ell_1=1,
+ \qquad \ell_m=2r_m\quad(m>1).
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ R_s:=\sum_{m\ge0}r_m(s)=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)},
+\]
+the three left-context cases contribute respectively
+\begin{equation}
+\begin{array}{c|c}
+ |\mathbf u|_1=0 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1=1 & R_s\\
+ |\mathbf u|_1>1 & 2(R_s-1)R_s
+\end{array}
+\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 2R_s^2.
+\label{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}
+\end{equation}
+In particular, the conflicting printed and corrected coefficients are
+\begin{equation}
+ \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2}
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2}.
+ \label{eq:dushistova-conflicting-constants}
+\end{equation}
+At \(s=\sigma_0\), these are \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Canonical regular words of denominator \(q\) parameterize the
+\(\phi_{\rm E}(q)\) reduced fractions in \((0,1)\).  Including the empty word
+and using the totient Dirichlet series therefore gives the displayed value
+of \(R_s\), which is finite for \(s>2\).  For \(m>1\), every canonical word
+of digit sum \(m\) has exactly two positive expansions: itself and the word
+obtained by replacing its final digit \(a\ge2\) by \(a-1,1\).  This terminal
+move preserves both digit sum and continuant, so \(\ell_m=2r_m\).  At the two
+endpoints, however, the empty word is the only word of sum zero, while
+\((1)\) is the only positive word of sum one and is not canonical.  This
+proves all four identities and the three contributions in
+\eqref{eq:left-context-endpoint-cases}.
+
+The precise loss in the published argument occurs in the proof of
+Dushistova's Lemma~7 \cite[pp.~668--669]{Dushistova2007}.  After separating
+the \(u=1\) term, the proof replaces the \(u>1\) left-context sum by twice a
+canonical convolution denoted there by \(\Sigma_2\).  In the displayed
+definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the restriction \(u>1\) has disappeared, so the
+empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\)
+case is not retained separately.  Thus the printed split contributes
+\(R_s+2R_s^2\), an excess of exactly \(R_s\).  Retaining the three endpoint
+classes gives \(R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2\).  This localization uses the
+same empty-continuant, final-digit, and exponent conventions as the published
+paper, so the discrepancy is not a normalization change.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Greedy moderate-block bound]
+\label{lem:greedy-moderate-block-bound}
+For \(s>2\), define
+\[
+ \eta_s(h):=
+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\\|\mathbf u|_1\ge h}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}
+\]
+and let \(G_s(N,h)\) be the total inverse-continuant weight of the words
+\(\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}\) with digit sum at least \(N\) and every
+digit smaller than \(h\).  For all sufficiently large \(h\),
+\begin{equation}
+ G_s(N,h)\le
+ \frac{L_s}{1-\eta_s(h)}
+ \eta_s(h)^{\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1},
+ \qquad L_s:=\sum_{\mathbf u\in\mathcal C_{\rm L}}
+ \mathcal K(\mathbf u)^{-s}=2R_s.
+ \label{eq:moderate-block-bound}
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
 \begin{proof}
+Scan a word from the left and close a block at the first digit for which the
+block's digit sum reaches \(h\); repeat, leaving the final remainder unclosed.
+This greedy factorization is unique.  Since every digit is smaller than
+\(h\), each closed block has digit sum in \([h,2h)\), and a word of digit sum
+at least \(N\) has at least \(\lfloor N/(2h)\rfloor-1\) closed blocks.
+The concatenation inequality makes the inverse-continuant weight at most the
+product of the block weights.  The greedy map is injective into sequences of
+closed blocks and one remainder.  Enlarging each closed-block class to all
+positive words of digit sum at least \(h\) gives mass \(\eta_s(h)\), while
+enlarging the remainder class gives mass \(L_s\).  Summing the resulting
+geometric series proves \eqref{eq:moderate-block-bound}; it applies for large
+\(h\) because absolute convergence gives \(\eta_s(h)\to0\).
+\end{proof}
+

The discrepancy is a narrow endpoint-bookkeeping error in Dushistova’s published proof, not a convention or normalization mismatch.

**Mathematical Resolution**

The evidence is the term-by-term comparison with Dushistova’s Theorem 3 and the specific decomposition in the proof of her Lemma 7, pp. 668–669:

- Dushistova sums over positive regular continued-fraction words \(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\) with \(a_t\ge2\), fixed digit sum \(a_1+\cdots+a_t=n\), and weight \(\mathcal K(\mathbf a)^{-2\beta}\).
- The new Proposition 6.4 proves that the canonical regular-to-negative conversion preserves the represented fraction and denominator and satisfies
  \[
  d(p/q)=a_1+\cdots+a_t-1.
  \]
  Hence, with \(s=2\beta\) and \(n=d+1\),
  \[
  \boxed{b_{2d+1}(s)=\sigma_{s/2}(d+1)}.
  \]
  The denominator, fixed-sum/cost, final-digit, empty-word, and exponent conventions are all compared explicitly in [sec_arithmetic_critical.tex](/D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_finite_window_zeckendorf_fibers_discrete_thermodynamics_tams/sec_arithmetic_critical.tex:53).
- The two leading coefficients are now displayed side by side:
  \[
  \boxed{\text{Dushistova: }R_s+2R_s^2},
  \qquad
  \boxed{\text{this paper: }2R_s^2},
  \qquad
  R_s=\frac{\zeta(s-1)}{\zeta(s)}.
  \]
  At \(s=\sigma_0\), these give \(10\) and \(8\), respectively.
- The new self-contained endpoint-correction Lemma 6.5 separates the left-context digit sums:
  \[
  u=0:R_s,\qquad u=1:R_s,\qquad u>1:2(R_s-1)R_s.
  \]
  Their sum is
  \[
  R_s+R_s+2(R_s-1)R_s=2R_s^2.
  \]
- The published proof separates the \(u=1\) contribution and then replaces the \(u>1\) contribution by twice its canonical convolution \(\Sigma_2\). In the displayed definition of \(\Sigma_2\), the \(u>1\) restriction is lost, so the empty canonical context \(u=0\) is included; meanwhile the original \(u=0\) case is no longer retained separately. The resulting excess is exactly \(R_s\). This localization, including the express disclaimer that it makes no claim about the rest of Dushistova’s paper, is in [sec_arithmetic_critical.tex](/D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_finite_window_zeckendorf_fibers_discrete_thermodynamics_tams/sec_arithmetic_critical.tex:105).

**Priority And Novelty**

Dushistova and Moshchevitin–Zhigljavsky now appear in the abstract, introduction, contribution boundary, contribution table, related-work audit, discussion immediately before Theorem 6.3, supplement discussion, and conclusion. Full bibliographic records and DOIs were added to [sec_references.tex](/D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_finite_window_zeckendorf_fibers_discrete_thermodynamics_tams/sec_references.tex:44) and `references.bib`.

The revised novelty claim is now:

> Dushistova previously treated the identical fixed-digit-sum continuant sum and its polynomial order, and stated a fuller expansion. This paper corrects her printed leading coefficient, gives a shorter context-sum proof of the corrected leading term, derives the critical heavy tail, and transfers it to the renewal/Fibonacci finite-size laws.

The manuscript does not claim priority for the local \(d^{-s}\) order or for Dushistova’s additional expansion coefficients. The settled attribution and recovery wording for Sidorov–Vershik, Lau–Ngai, Feng–Olivier, and Feng remains intact, and the existing recovery propositions remain recovery propositions. The revised contribution boundary and related-work discussion are in [sec_introduction.tex](/D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_finite_window_zeckendorf_fibers_discrete_thermodynamics_tams/sec_introduction.tex:358).

The anti-cheating dependency boundary is preserved. Theorem 6.3 remains a separate arithmetic theorem proved from continued-fraction conversion, finite context sums, continuant inequalities, dominated convergence, and the large/moderate-digit decomposition. It assumes no renewal theorem or regularly varying tail. Regular variation is derived only afterward in Theorem 6.7.

The referee’s proof-completeness repairs were also applied:

- Dominated convergence now has an explicit indicator on the fixed context space and handles the empty right context.
- Lemma 6.6 formalizes the greedy moderate-block factorization, its injection, and the enlargement to arbitrary blocks.
- The exactly-one-large-digit contribution now has the explicit bound
  \[
  2L_s\sum_{h\le a\le n/2}a^{-s}G_s(n/4,h).
  \]
- The oscillation statement is restricted to the leading term and explicitly permits lower-order oscillations.
- The renewal result cites Omey–Van Gulck, Section 3.2, first displayed renewal asymptotic, and verifies nonnegative integer increments, finite mean, regular variation, and span one using costs \(3\) and \(5\).
- The stable-law location convention is fixed by
  \[
  \log\mathbb E e^{it\mathcal S_\alpha}
  =\int_0^\infty(e^{itx}-1-itx)\alpha x^{-\alpha-1}\,dx.
  \]
